title: Preface
summary: This text is the cover page and table of contents of a January 2021 document published by the Turkish Ministry of Commerce's General Directorate of Consumer Protection and Market Surveillance. It presents Law No. 6502 on Consumer Protection and its comprehensive secondary legislation. The table of contents lists all covered regulations, including: unfair contract terms, installment sales, consumer credit, housing finance, prepaid housing sales, building completion insurance, off-premises and distance contracts (including financial services), timeshare and package travel contracts, subscription contracts, promotional practices, price labels, user manuals, warranty certificates, after-sales services, consumer awards, commercial advertising and unfair practices, advertising/consumer councils, consumer arbitration boards (including rapporteurship, expertise, and fee schedules), refurbished product sales, administrative fine settlements, financial consumer fees, 2021 administrative fines, monetary limits, and gross income determination. Contact information (ALO 175 helpline, websites, social media) is also provided.

title: BİRİNCİ KISIM
key_items: Satıştan kaçınma; Sipariş edilmeyen mal veya hizmetler
summary: This text covers Part 1 (Purpose, Scope, Definitions) and Part 2 (General Principles) of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. Part 1 defines the law's purpose (protecting consumer health, safety, economic interests, environmental protection, awareness, and voluntary organizations), its scope (all consumer transactions), and key definitions (Minister, service, importer, goods, seller, consumer, producer, etc.). Part 2 establishes: (1) Basic principles requiring contracts in clear 12pt language, prohibiting unfavorable mid-contract changes, extra charges, and compound interest; mandating fee disclosure; regulating promissory notes and personal guarantees; and including participation banks. (2) Unfair terms: defining them as non-negotiated, imbalanced clauses; declaring them void; requiring clear language with consumer-favorable interpretation; and empowering the Ministry to remove them. (3) Refusal to sell: prohibiting refusal of displayed goods, unjustified service refusal, and tying conditions. (4) Unsolicited goods/services: no rights can be claimed, silence is not acceptance, and the burden of proof lies with the claimant.

title: ÜÇÜNCÜ KISIM
key_items: Ayıplı Mal ve Hizmetler BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Ayıplı Mallar
summary: This text covers Part Three of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law, addressing defective goods and services. For defective goods (Articles 8-12): it defines defective goods as those not conforming to contract, lacking promised features, or containing material/legal/economic deficiencies, including late delivery and improper assembly. It establishes seller's delivery obligation, burden of proof (6-month presumption of defect at delivery), labeling requirements, and consumer's alternative rights (contract termination, price reduction, free repair, replacement) with joint liability among seller, manufacturer, and importer, 30/60-day deadlines, and immediate refund provisions. Statute of limitations is 2 years (5 for real estate), with no limitation for concealed defects. For defective services (Articles 13-16): it defines defective services, establishes provider's performance obligation, consumer's rights (re-performance, repair, price reduction, termination), proportionality limits, 30-day deadline, and a 2-year statute of limitations, with no limitation for fraud or gross negligence.

title: DÖRDÜNCÜ KISIM
key_items: Tüketici Sözleşmeleri BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Taksitle Satış
summary: This text covers Part Four, Section One of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law on installment sales contracts. Article 17 defines installment sales (seller delivers goods/services, consumer pays in parts), extends rules to financial leasing with mandatory ownership transfer, and requires written form for validity, prohibiting sellers from later invoking invalidity against consumers. Article 18 grants consumers a 7-day unconditional withdrawal right, requires sellers to prove consumer notification, limits goods use to normal inspection, excludes withdrawal for services started with consent and for financial leasing. Article 19 regulates default: sellers may accelerate the full remaining debt only after fulfilling all obligations and if the consumer misses at least two consecutive installments (≥1/10 of remaining debt) or one installment (≥1/4), with a mandatory 30-day notice; interest and commissions are excluded from acceleration calculations. Article 20 allows early full or partial payment with proportional interest/commission reduction. Article 21 applies Turkish Code of Obligations prepayment rules for contracts exceeding one year or indefinite, and delegates detailed procedures to regulation.

title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
summary: This text covers Chapter 2 of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law on Consumer Credits (Articles 22-31). It defines consumer credit contracts and credit card agreements, mandates written form, and requires pre-contract information disclosure. It establishes a 14-day withdrawal right with specific repayment conditions, mandates fixed interest rates for term loans, and sets consequences for missing rate information. Contract modifications are restricted: term loan terms cannot be changed against the consumer, while indefinite-term loans require 30-day written notice for rate changes. Consumers may repay early with proportional cost reductions. Default acceleration requires the lender to have fulfilled all obligations, the consumer to miss at least two consecutive installments, and a 30-day notice. Insurance cannot be imposed without the consumer's explicit request. Linked credits are defined with criteria for economic unity, joint liability among seller, provider, and lender, and withdrawal rights. Finally, it prohibits fees on credit-linked accounts, bans unauthorized linked deposit contracts, requires a no-fee credit card option, and delegates detailed procedures to regulations.

title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Konut Finansmanı

nodes.title: Konut finansmanı sözleşmeleri
nodes.summary: This text is from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law, Chapter Three on Housing Finance. Article 32 defines housing finance contracts as agreements covering: credit for acquiring housing, financial leasing of housing to consumers, credit secured by consumer-owned housing, and refinancing of such credits. It mandates that housing finance contracts must be in writing to be valid, and prohibits housing finance institutions from later invoking the contract's invalidity to the consumer's detriment. Article 33 establishes a pre-contract information obligation, requiring housing finance institutions to provide consumers with a pre-contract information form detailing the contract terms a reasonable time before the contract is concluded.

nodes.title: Temerrüt
nodes.summary: The text covers two articles from a Turkish consumer protection law on housing finance. Article 34 (Default) stipulates that a housing finance institution may demand full repayment only after fulfilling all obligations and the consumer missing at least two consecutive installments, with a 30-day notice. Interest and commissions are excluded from accelerated installment calculations. In financial leasing, if the consumer fails to perform, the institution must terminate the contract, obtain a valuation from authorized persons, notify the consumer at least 10 business days before sale, sell as a prudent merchant, and pay any excess to the consumer. Post-sale, occupants must vacate; otherwise, enforcement proceedings apply. Article 35 (Linked Loans) defines linked loan contracts where a loan is exclusively for a specific housing purchase forming economic unity. It establishes joint liability of seller and institution for non-delivery, limits institutional liability to one year and the loan amount, maintains liability even after loan transfer to other entities, and excludes consumer-selected housing purchases from linked loan classification.

nodes.title: Faiz oranı
nodes.summary: Article 36 defines interest rates for loans and financial leasing. It states that the portion of repayments (loans) or rent (leasing) exceeding principal is considered interest. For housing finance loans and financial leasing, interest rates may be set as fixed, variable, or a combination, as specified in the contract. Fixed rates, set at contract formation, cannot be altered without mutual consent. Variable rates may be adjusted based on the lowest widely accepted domestic or foreign index specified in the contract, provided periodic payments do not exceed the maximum stated in the contract. Consumers must be informed of potential effects when variable rates apply. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey determines the reference interest rates and indices that may be used.

nodes.title: Erken ödeme
nodes.summary: The text covers Turkish consumer protection law provisions on housing finance and pre-paid housing sales. Article 37 addresses early payment: consumers may pay installments or the full debt early, with mandatory interest/cost reductions; early payment compensation is capped at 1% (remaining term ≤36 months) or 2% (>36 months) for fixed rates, and prohibited for variable rates. Article 38 prohibits imposing insurance without the consumer's explicit written request and requires acceptance of the consumer's chosen insurer. Article 39 bans fees on loan-dedicated accounts, prohibits credit deposit agreements without explicit instruction, extends consumer status to housing cooperative members, and delegates procedural details to regulations. Article 40 defines pre-paid housing sale contracts, mandates a pre-information form at least one day before signing, and requires a building permit. Article 41 stipulates that pre-paid sales must be registered in the land registry and sale-promise contracts executed at a notary; sellers cannot invoke invalidity against consumers, and no payments or debt documents may be demanded before a valid contract exists.

nodes.title: Consumer Protection: Housing Finance Insurance, Prepaid Sales, and Formal Requirements
nodes.summary: The text covers provisions from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law on housing finance and prepaid housing sales. It includes: limits on early payment compensation (1% or 2% based on remaining term); Article 38 requiring the consumer's explicit request for insurance and mandating acceptance of any insurer's coverage; Article 39 prohibiting fees on dedicated accounts, banning unauthorized credit agreements, extending consumer status to cooperative members, and delegating procedural rules to regulations; Article 40 defining prepaid housing sales contracts, mandating a pre-information form at least one day before signing, and requiring a building permit; and Article 41 stipulating formal requirements such as land registry registration or notarial execution, and prohibiting sellers from demanding payments or debt documents before a valid contract exists.

nodes.title: Prepayment Housing Sales: Guarantees, Withdrawal Rights, and Delivery
nodes.summary: The text covers three articles from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law on prepayment housing sales. Article 42 requires sellers of large projects to obtain building completion insurance or equivalent guarantees before starting sales; these guarantees are protected from bankruptcy, seizure, and precautionary measures. Article 43 grants consumers a 14-day right to withdraw from the contract without reason or penalty, obliges sellers to prove consumer notification, stipulates that linked loan contracts take effect only after the withdrawal period, prohibits charging any fees during this period, and requires consumers to return possessions within 10 days of receiving refunds. Article 44 limits the transfer or delivery period to a maximum of 36 months from the contract date, with land registry registration of co-ownership constituting delivery.

nodes.title: Sözleşmeden dönme MADDE 45- (1) (Değişik: 2/1/2017-KHK-684/8 md.; Aynen kabul: 1/2/2018-7074/8 md.)
nodes.summary: Article 45 of the Consumer Protection Law covers the right to terminate a prepayment housing sales contract. Consumers may terminate within 24 months of the contract date without providing a reason. Upon termination, the seller may claim tax/fee costs plus tiered compensation (2% for 0-3 months, 4% for 3-6 months, 6% for 6-12 months, 8% for 12-24 months) of the contract price. No charges apply if the seller fails to fulfill obligations, the consumer dies, permanently loses income, or the seller refuses to replace the contract with an installment sale. The seller must refund all amounts and return any debt-creating documents within 180 days of the termination notice reaching the seller. The consumer must return their acquisitions within 10 days of receiving the refund and documents.

Diğer hususlar

summary: This section of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law governs housing finance and pre-paid housing sales. It defines housing finance contracts (credit, leasing, secured credit, refinancing), mandates written form and pre-contract information. It regulates default procedures, including accelerated repayment conditions and financial leasing termination. Linked loan contracts establish joint seller-institution liability. Interest rates may be fixed, variable, or combined, with Central Bank reference indices. Early payment compensation is capped at 1-2%; insurance requires explicit consumer consent. Pre-paid housing sales require a building permit, pre-information form, land registry registration, and notarial execution. Large projects need completion insurance protected from bankruptcy. Consumers enjoy a 14-day withdrawal right and may terminate within 24 months with tiered compensation (2-8%). Delivery is limited to 36 months. Procedural details are delegated to regulations.

title: Diğer Tüketici Sözleşmeleri

nodes.title: Diğer Tüketici Sözleşmeleri (intro)
nodes.summary: Article 47 defines off-premises consumer contracts as those concluded outside business premises with simultaneous physical presence, immediately after such meetings, or during organized promotional trips. Key provisions include: contracts must be made by Ministry-authorized sellers; consumers must receive clear information before being bound (burden of proof on seller); contracts are invalid unless in writing, with the seller required to obtain the consumer's handwritten date and signature, provide a copy, and deliver goods/services; consumers enjoy a 14-day withdrawal right without reason or penalty, during which sellers cannot demand payment; consumers are not liable for damage from normal use; if the seller fails obligations or omits withdrawal information, the 14-day limit is extended up to one year after expiry; and mandatory content, exclusions, direct sales rules, rights, obligations, delivery, and seller qualifications are determined by regulation.

nodes.title: Mesafeli sözleşmeler
nodes.summary: The text covers three articles of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. Article 48 defines distance contracts (concluded without physical presence via remote communication), mandates pre-contract consumer information, sets a 30-day maximum delivery period, grants a 14-day unconditional withdrawal right, and imposes record-keeping duties on intermediaries. Article 49 addresses distance contracts for financial services (banking, credit, insurance, pension, investment, payment), requiring clear pre-contract disclosure, written confirmation of terms, the right to a paper copy, a 14-day withdrawal right, and simplified termination procedures. Article 50 governs timeshare and long-term holiday service contracts, defining them, requiring pre-contract information forms, mandating handwritten dates and signatures, granting a 14-day withdrawal right (extending to linked credit agreements), requiring building completion insurance for large projects, allowing pre-paid sale withdrawal with up to 2% compensation, capping delivery at 36 months, and delegating detailed rules to regulations.

nodes.title: Paket tur sözleşmeleri
nodes.summary: Article 51 defines package tour contracts as agreements selling at least two services (transport, accommodation, or other tourism services) together at an all-inclusive price, lasting over 24 hours or including overnight stay. It applies regardless of who determines tour details or if services are billed separately. If the organizer lacks a Turkish representative, the agent assumes organizer-level liability. A pre-contract brochure is mandatory, and written/distance contracts must be provided to the consumer. Consumers may accept alternatives or terminate the contract if essential elements change or the tour is cancelled pre-departure, with full refund. Consumers can request price reductions for deficiencies and terminate if the organizer fails key obligations, with immediate refund (minus charges for services already rendered). The organizer is liable for all damages from non-performance, including compensation for wasted vacation time. Commercial users are also protected as consumers. Implementation details are delegated to regulation.

nodes.title: Abonelik sözleşmeleri
nodes.summary: The text covers two articles from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. Article 52 defines subscription agreements as contracts for continuous or regular acquisition of goods/services. It mandates written or distance-based formation with a copy provided to the consumer, prohibits auto-renewal clauses in fixed-term contracts, and grants consumers the right to terminate indefinite or over-one-year contracts without penalty. It requires sellers to fulfill termination requests within regulatory deadlines, refund remaining fees within 15 days, and maintain systems for processing termination requests. Article 53 regulates promotional practices by periodical publications, restricting promotions to culturally relevant goods/services, setting duration limits (75 days for daily, 18 weeks for weekly, 12 months for longer publications), requiring delivery within 45 days post-promotion, prohibiting price increases or consumer payment for promotional items, banning splitting of promotional items, and extending these rules to promotions indirectly linked to periodicals. Both articles defer detailed procedures to regulations.

summary: This section covers 'Other Consumer Contracts' under Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. It addresses: off-premises contracts (Art. 47) requiring written form, seller-authorized sales, burden of proof on sellers, and 14-day withdrawal rights; distance contracts (Arts. 48–50) for general goods, financial services, and timeshare/long-term holiday services, mandating pre-contract disclosure, 14-day withdrawal, delivery limits, record-keeping, and completion insurance; package tour contracts (Art. 51) defining bundled tourism services, consumer termination and refund rights, price reduction claims, and organizer liability for non-performance including wasted vacation time; and subscription agreements (Arts. 52–53) governing continuous service contracts with termination rights, refund obligations, plus promotional practices by periodicals with duration, delivery, and pricing restrictions. All provisions delegate detailed implementation to regulations.

nodes.title: Fiyat etiketi
nodes.summary: The text covers Articles 54-57 of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. Article 54 mandates price labels on retail goods showing all taxes, unit price, and production details, with consumer-favorable pricing when discrepancies exist; discounted sales must display original prices with proof burden on sellers; oversight falls to the Ministry, municipalities, and chambers. Article 55 requires Turkish-language user manuals covering introduction, use, installation, maintenance, and repair, with safety warnings for hazardous products; manufacturers/importers prepare manuals while sellers ensure delivery. Article 56 obligates manufacturers/importers to issue warranty certificates with a minimum two-year period; if a product malfunctions again during warranty, consumers may exercise alternative rights (replacement, refund), with joint liability among seller, manufacturer, and importer. Article 57 defines voluntary warranty as additional commitments beyond legal rights, prohibiting charges to consumers for exercising such rights during the commitment period. All articles delegate specific implementation details to regulations.

nodes.title: Consumer Protection: Pricing, Use Manuals, and Warranty Certificates
nodes.summary: The page concludes a pricing/discount article (Ministry, municipalities, and chambers oversee compliance; regulations govern labels, tariffs, and discounted-sale procedures). Article 55 mandates Turkish introduction and use manuals for goods, covering use, installation, maintenance, and simple repair, with international symbols where needed. Safety and health/environment hazard warnings must appear clearly in Turkish. Manufacturers/importers prepare manuals; sellers deliver and prove delivery. Regulations specify applicable goods and minimum elements. Article 56 requires manufacturers/importers to issue warranty certificates, with sellers completing and handing them to consumers. Minimum warranty is two years from delivery, though the Ministry may set alternative units. If goods malfunction again after a repair, consumers may invoke other Article 11 remedies; sellers cannot refuse, and seller, manufacturer, and importer bear joint liability. Regulations determine which goods require warranty certificates.

nodes.title: İhtiyari garanti
nodes.summary: The text covers four articles from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. Article 57 defines voluntary guarantees as additional commitments (exchange, repair, maintenance, refund) by sellers, manufacturers, or importers, preserving consumers' legal rights. It prohibits charging consumers for using guaranteed rights, requires guarantors to be bound by their advertising, mandates written delivery, and specifies required content (conditions, duration, contact info). Article 58 addresses after-sales services: manufacturers/importers must provide maintenance and repair during the product's useful life, obtain service qualification certificates, respect maximum repair times, and may use own or third-party service stations while remaining responsible. If an importer ceases operations, seller, manufacturer, and new importer share joint liability. Article 59 mandates consumer awareness education in school curricula and requires national radio/TV to broadcast at least 15 minutes monthly (08:00–22:00) on consumer awareness, monitored by RTÜK. Article 60 defines consumer awards as incentives for consumer protection, awareness, and exercising legal rights.

nodes.title: Voluntary Guarantees, After-Sales Services, and Consumer Awareness
nodes.summary: The page covers three topics from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. First, it concludes the voluntary guarantee section, stating that guarantors are bound by their advertisements, must include consumer rights, conditions, and contact info, and must provide guarantees in writing or via permanent data storage; guarantees bind even if not fully compliant. Second, Article 58 (After-Sales Services) requires producers/importers to provide maintenance and repair during the ministry-determined useful life, obtain approved service certificates, respect maximum repair times at authorized stations, and may use existing service organizations. Independent service stations are also liable to consumers. If an importer ceases operations, the seller, producer, and new importer are jointly liable during the warranty period, and the producer/new importer must serve the full useful life thereafter. Third, Article 59 (Consumer Awareness) mandates adding consumer education to school curricula via the Ministry of Education and requires national radio/TV stations to broadcast at least 15 minutes monthly (08:00–22:00) on consumer awareness, with reports filed to the RTÜK.

nodes.title: Tüketici ödülleri
nodes.summary: Article 60 of the Consumer Protection Law defines consumer awards as prizes intended to encourage consumers to protect their rights, raise awareness, or exercise their legal rights. It stipulates that consumer awards and similarly named prizes must be granted without any benefit being obtained and must be based on previously announced objective criteria. The procedures and principles governing the granting of consumer awards are to be determined by regulation.

summary: This section covers Articles 54–60 of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law on informing consumers and protecting their interests. It addresses: mandatory price labels displaying taxes, unit prices, and original prices for discounted goods (Art. 54); Turkish-language user manuals with safety warnings, prepared by manufacturers/importers and delivered by sellers (Art. 55); warranty certificates with a minimum two-year period and joint liability among seller, manufacturer, and importer (Art. 56); voluntary guarantees as additional commitments that must be in writing, bound by advertising, and free of charge to consumers (Art. 57); after-sales services requiring maintenance and repair during the product's useful life, service qualification certificates, and maximum repair times (Art. 58); consumer awareness education in school curricula and mandatory 15-minute monthly radio/TV broadcasts monitored by RTÜK (Art. 59); and consumer awards as incentives for exercising rights, based on objective criteria (Art. 60). Implementation details are delegated to regulations.

title: Ticari Reklam ve Haksız Ticari Uygulamalar
summary: The text covers three articles of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. Article 61 defines commercial advertising, mandates compliance with ethics, public order, and truthfulness; prohibits misleading, exploitative, or harmful ads and covert advertising; permits comparative advertising; and places the burden of proof on advertisers, agencies, and media. Article 62 defines unfair commercial practices as those lacking professional diligence that significantly distort consumer behavior, deems deceptive or aggressive practices unfair, prohibits them, and assigns the burden of proof to the commercial entity. Article 63 establishes the Advertising Board (19 members from government ministries, professional associations, consumer organizations, and academia) with authority to set principles, investigate, and impose penalties including suspension, correction, fines, or up to three months' suspension. It details the Board's composition, three-year terms, quorum (11 members), majority voting, specialized committees, expert consultation, and publication of decisions by the Ministry.

title: YEDİNCİ KISIM Tüketici Kuruluşları BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Tüketici Konseyi ve Reklam Konseyi
summary: This text covers Part 7 (Consumer Organizations), Section 1 of a Turkish consumer protection law, detailing two councils. Article 64 establishes the Consumer Council, which meets at least annually under the Ministry's coordination to identify consumer problems and needs, protect their interests, and submit opinions to relevant authorities on the Law's application. Article 65 establishes the Advertising Council, which meets at least annually under the Ministry's coordination to develop advertising policies, track modern communication practices, conduct research on the advertising sector and its supervision, and forward opinions and suggestions to relevant authorities. Both councils share common rules: public institution representatives may not exceed 50% of total membership, and their members, working procedures, and other operational details are to be determined by regulation.

title: Tüketici Hakem Heyeti
summary: This text covers Articles 66-72 of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law, detailing the Consumer Arbitration Board (Tüketici Hakem Heyeti). Article 66 establishes the Board's composition (five members: chair, municipality, bar, chamber of commerce/artisan, and consumer organization representatives) and jurisdiction in provincial/district centers. Article 67 defines rapporteurs' roles in preparing files and reports. Article 68 sets mandatory application thresholds (4,000 TL for district, 6,000 TL for province), application locations, and annual monetary adjustments. Article 69 grants the Board authority to request information and documents. Article 70 addresses binding decisions, prohibition of attorney fees, 15-day objection period to consumer courts, finality of court rulings, fee allocation (Ministry covers costs against consumers; collects from opposing party in consumer's favor). Article 71 specifies attendance fees determined by the Ministry with Finance Ministry approval. Article 72 delegates operational procedures, rapporteur qualifications, and expert witness rules to regulations.

title: SEKİZİNCİ KISIM

nodes.title: MADDE 73
nodes.summary: This text covers Article 73 of the Consumer Protection Law, detailing the jurisdiction and procedures of consumer courts. Key points include: consumer courts handle disputes from consumer transactions and practices; cases filed by the Ministry, consumers, or consumer organizations are exempt from court fees; expert and attorney fees in cases filed by consumer organization umbrella bodies are covered by the Ministry or collected from the defendant; proceedings follow the Code of Civil Procedure (Law No. 6100); cases may be filed at the consumer's residence; consumer organizations, public institutions, and the Ministry may seek precautionary measures or file cases to prevent violations generally affecting consumers (excluding unfair commercial practices and advertising); plaintiffs in general consumer cases may request publication of decisions in at least three national newspapers at the defendant's expense; and final court decisions are transmitted to the Ministry via the National Judiciary Network, while decisions on objections to arbitration committee rulings are sent back to the relevant committee.

nodes.title: Dava şartı olarak arabuluculuk MADDE 73/A- (Ek:22/7/2020-7251/59 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers two Turkish consumer law provisions. Article 73/A establishes mediation as a mandatory precondition for filing lawsuits in consumer courts, listing exceptions (arbitration board disputes, objections to their decisions, specific Article 73(6) and 74 cases, and real estate disputes). It states that a specific mediation law provision cannot be applied against consumers, that mediation fees are covered by the Ministry of Justice budget in certain circumstances (capped at a two-hour fee), and that if the consumer prevails, the fee is collected from the defendant. Article 74 addresses stopping production/sales and seizing defective serial goods: the Ministry, consumers, or consumer organizations may sue to halt sales, eliminate defects, and recall goods. Courts may order temporary sales suspension or defect correction. Producers/importers must fix defects within three months or recall and destroy goods. Consumer rights to sue and claim damages remain intact, and product safety legislation applies when defects endanger consumer safety.

nodes.title: Consumer Protection Law: Inspection and Product Service Supervision
nodes.summary: The text covers Articles 75 and 76 of the Consumer Protection Law under the Inspection section. Article 75 authorizes Ministry inspectors, customs and trade inspectors, and assigned personnel to conduct inspections, investigations, and research wherever goods or services are provided. It requires authorized persons and organizations to furnish accurate information and documents (originals or certified copies) upon request. Article 76 defines consumer products as any new, used, or refurbished items designed or reasonably expected for consumer use, including service-sector items, obtained via commercial or other means. Antiques and second-hand items needing repair or modification before use are excluded if the producer/distributor clearly informs the consumer. Consumer products and services must not endanger life, property safety, or the environment and must comply with all mandatory administrative and technical regulations. The Ministry is responsible for market surveillance and inspection of consumer products under the Technical Legislation Law.

nodes.title: Ceza hükümleri (1)
nodes.summary: Article 77 of the Turkish Consumer Protection Law outlines administrative penalty provisions for violations of various articles. It specifies tiered fines (ranging from 200 TL to 5 million TL) based on the type and severity of violations, including unfair contract terms, housing delivery failures, product sales, advertising violations, pyramid schemes, and unfair commercial practices. Separate penalties apply to media channels (TV, radio, internet, SMS) with higher fines for nationwide broadcasts. Repeat offenses within a year may incur up to tenfold fines. The article also sets annual fine caps tied to 5% of gross income (or 5/1000 of equity for financial institutions), mandates suspension of campaigns for periodic publications, and allows the Advertising Board to impose combined or separate sanctions. It references criminal law for pyramid schemes, provides a 7-day compliance notice for information violations, and states that administrative penalties do not preclude other legal actions. The Ministry retains authority to resolve ambiguities in application.

nodes.title: Uzlaşma MADDE 77/A- (Ek:28/11/2017-7061/116 md.)
nodes.summary: Article 77/A (added 28/11/2017) establishes a settlement mechanism for administrative fines. The Ministry may settle with the penalized party when violations stem from misinterpretation of laws or disagreement between court decisions and administration. Settlement applies to fines issued by the Ministry and governorates, excluding Advertising Board fines. Requests must be filed within 15 days of notification, before any administrative court appeal; filing suspends the lawsuit period, and no second request is permitted if settlement fails. Settlement commissions evaluate requests; their records are final and immediately enforceable, and the penalized party waives the right to sue or complain. The maximum discount is 50%, and no additional prepayment discount under Law 5326/17 applies. The settlement record is notified immediately and must be paid within 15 days. Commission members' honoraria are set by the Ministry with Finance Ministry approval. Procedures for commission establishment and operations are governed by a regulation.

nodes.title: Cezalarda yetki ve itiraz
nodes.summary: Article 78 of the Consumer Protection Law covers authority and appeals for administrative penalties. It specifies which body issues penalties: the Ministry handles those under certain paragraphs of Article 77, the Advertising Board's decisions are enforced by the Ministry, and other penalties are issued by the governor's office where the entity's center is located. It establishes that administrative penalty decisions can be appealed to administrative courts under Law No. 2577, with a 30-day filing deadline from the day following notification, and that filing a lawsuit does not suspend enforcement of the decision. Finally, it mandates that administrative fines must be paid within one month of notification.

summary: This section (Eighth Part) of the Turkish Consumer Protection Law covers consumer court procedures, mediation requirements, product supervision, and administrative penalties. It details consumer court jurisdiction, fee exemptions, precautionary measures, and publication of decisions (Art. 73). It establishes mandatory mediation as a precondition for lawsuits with specific exceptions, and provisions for halting sales and recalling defective goods (Art. 73/A, 74). It authorizes inspections, defines consumer products, and mandates market surveillance (Arts. 75-76). It outlines tiered administrative fines for various violations, including unfair contracts, advertising, and pyramid schemes, with caps tied to gross income (Art. 77). It provides a settlement mechanism allowing up to 50% fine reduction (Art. 77/A). Finally, it specifies which authority issues penalties and establishes 30-day appeal deadlines to administrative courts (Art. 78).

title: DOKUZUNCU KISIM Çeşitli Hükümler
summary: This text covers the final provisions (Part 9) of Turkey's Consumer Protection Law. It addresses: (1) prohibition of food imitation products that could endanger consumer safety, with exceptions for traditional handicrafts bearing warning labels; (2) definition and prohibition of pyramid sales schemes, with Ministry authority to investigate and shut down electronic systems; (3) use of official/private labs for testing, with costs borne by the Ministry or recovered from non-compliant producers; (4) budget allocation for consumer protection bodies; (5) application of general rules where the law is silent; (6) Ministry's authority to issue regulations within six months, consulting relevant institutions and NGOs; (7) establishment of new staff positions; (8) repeal of the old 1995 Consumer Protection Law (No. 4077); (9) transitional provisions for ongoing cases, pre-existing contracts, limitation periods, and continued application of old regulations until new ones are issued; (10) exclusion of mediation requirements for already-pending cases; (11) entry into force six months after publication; and (12) execution by the Council of Ministers.

summary: This text is a reference list from Turkey's Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502), detailing the effective dates of amendments and repeals made by subsequent legislation. nodes.title: Unfair Terms in Consumer Contracts Regulation – Purpose, Scope, Definitions
nodes.summary: This page presents the First Chapter of the Regulation on Unfair Terms in Consumer Contracts (Official Gazette, 17 June 2014, No. 29033). Article 1 (Purpose) establishes that the regulation governs procedures for detecting and monitoring unfair terms in consumer contracts. Article 2 (Scope) states it covers all unfair terms in consumer contracts, including those prepared by entities operating under legal permits. Article 3 (Legal Basis) cites Articles 5 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 (7 November 2013). Article 4 (Definitions) defines key terms: Ministry (Customs and Trade), General Directorate (Consumer Protection and Market Surveillance), unfair term (non-negotiated clause creating imbalance against the consumer), service, court (consumer court), goods (tangible, real estate, and intangible items), contract (written or oral), contract drafter (commercial or professional entity), consumer (non-commercial individual or entity), and consumer organizations (associations, foundations, or their umbrella bodies).

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM Genel Esaslar
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 (General Principles) of a Turkish consumer protection regulation, addressing unfair contract terms. Article 5 defines unfair terms as those not negotiated with the consumer and creating an imbalance contrary to good faith. It presumes pre-prepared standard terms are non-negotiated, places the burden of proof on the drafter, and notes that negotiating one term does not exempt the rest of a standard contract from regulation. An annex lists example unfair terms (non-exhaustive). Article 6 states that unfairness is assessed at the time of contract formation, considering the nature of goods/services and other clauses. It prohibits evaluating the balance between main obligations or market value versus price if terms are clear. Written terms must be in clear, understandable language, and ambiguous terms are interpreted in the consumer's favor. Article 7 declares unfair terms absolutely void while preserving the validity of remaining contract terms, and prevents the drafter from claiming they would not have contracted without the void terms.

nodes.title: Haksız Şartların Denetimi
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 (Supervision of Unfair Terms) and Chapter 4 (Final Provisions) of the Turkish Regulation on Unfair Terms in Consumer Contracts. Article 8 outlines the Ministry's authority to require removal of unfair terms from standard consumer contracts, granting a 30-day deadline (extendable to 90 days) for contract preparers to comply. It states that if unfair terms are declared void and communicated to consumers in writing or electronically, they are deemed removed from existing valid contracts. Administrative fines apply per contract if terms are not removed within the deadline. Article 9 repeals the previous regulation dated 13/6/2003 (Official Gazette No. 25137). Article 10 specifies the regulation enters into force on its publication date. Article 11 assigns execution authority to the Minister of Customs and Trade.

summary: This section presents the Turkish Regulation on Unfair Terms in Consumer Contracts (Official Gazette, 17 June 2014, No. 29033), based on Consumer Protection Law No. 6502. It covers: (1) Purpose, scope, and definitions of key terms including unfair term, consumer, contract drafter, and relevant institutions; (2) General principles defining unfair terms as non-negotiated clauses creating imbalance contrary to good faith, establishing burden of proof on the drafter, assessment criteria at contract formation, clear language requirements, consumer-favorable interpretation of ambiguity, and absolute voidness of unfair terms while preserving remaining contract validity; (3) Supervision procedures granting the Ministry authority to mandate removal of unfair terms within 30–90 days, with administrative fines for non-compliance; and (4) Final provisions repealing the 2003 regulation, specifying entry into force upon publication, and assigning execution to the Minister of Customs and Trade.

title: EK -1

nodes.title: Haksız Sözleşme Şartları
nodes.summary: This text is Annex 1 (EK-1) of a Turkish regulation on unfair terms in consumer contracts. It defines unfair contract terms in paragraph (1), listing 17 categories (a–q) of clauses that are deemed unfair, including: limiting organizer liability for death/injury; eliminating consumer legal rights; one-sided performance obligations; asymmetric cancellation and retention rights; disproportionate penalties; arbitrary termination; indefinite contract termination without notice; automatic renewal; irrevocable acceptance of unknown terms; unilateral modification of terms, product nature, or price; exclusive conformity determination; limiting agent commitments; forcing consumer performance despite organizer non-performance; unauthorized assignment of rights; and restricting consumer access to courts or legal remedies. Paragraph (2) provides specific exceptions and applicability rules for sub-clauses (f), (h), and (i), allowing financial services unilateral termination with immediate notification, permitting price index clauses if the method is specified, and excluding securities, financial instruments, and foreign currency transactions from these provisions.

nodes.title: TAKSİTLE SATIŞ SÖZLEŞMELERİ HAKKINDA YÖNETMELİK BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Regulation on Installment Sales Contracts (Official Gazette, Jan 14, 2015, No. 29236). It covers: (1) Purpose – establishing procedures and principles for installment sales contracts; (2) Scope – applicable to consumer installment sales and financial leasing contracts requiring ownership transfer at lease end, with special provisions for participation banks; prepaid installment sales fall under the Turkish Code of Obligations, and credit card purchases are excluded; (3) Legal basis – grounded in Articles 21 and 84 of Consumer Protection Law No. 6502; (4) Definitions – defining key terms including early payment, financial leasing contract, service, permanent data storage, commission, goods (tangible, real estate, and intangible), payment plan, provider, seller, installment, installment sales contract, installment due date, and consumer.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 of a regulation on installment sales contracts, addressing the contract's form and mandatory content. Article 5 requires the contract to be in written form, provided to the consumer on paper or permanent storage, in at least 12-point font, clear and readable language. A free copy may be requested later. The contract is invalid without written form, and the seller cannot invoke invalidity to the consumer's detriment. Article 6 lists mandatory content: parties' identification details, contract date, delivery date, subject goods/services, cash and installment prices (tax-inclusive, in TL), withdrawal right details, payment plan, early payment and interest reduction rights, interest rates (including late payment capped at 30% above contract rate), default consequences, and consumer dispute resolution options. For financial leasing contracts, additional requirements include ownership transfer conditions, end-of-term transfer terms, receivable assignment provisions, and insurance details.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of the Regulation on Installment Sales Contracts, addressing the consumer's right of withdrawal and its consequences. Article 7 establishes that consumers may withdraw from installment sales contracts within seven days without reason or penalty. It specifies when the withdrawal period begins (contract date for services, delivery date for goods), allows withdrawal between contract and delivery, and applies goods-delivery rules to combined contracts. Written or permanent-data notice suffices, and the seller bears the burden of proving the consumer was informed. Consumers may only inspect goods normally; regular use or consented service commencement voids the right. Financial leasing transactions are excluded. Article 8 outlines consequences: the seller must refund all payments and return debt documents within seven days of receiving the withdrawal notice at no cost to the consumer; the consumer must return the goods within seven days or be deemed to have not withdrawn; and the consumer bears the return shipping costs.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter Four of a Turkish regulation on installment sales contracts, addressing three topics: (1) Consumer default (Article 9): The seller may demand full payment only if all obligations are fulfilled and the consumer defaults on at least two consecutive installments totaling 1/10 of remaining debt, or one installment totaling 1/4 of remaining debt. A written 30-day maturity notice is required, and interest/commissions are excluded from calculations. (2) Early payment (Article 10): Consumers may pay the full amount or one/more upcoming installments early; the seller must apply proportional interest and commission reductions. (3) Issuance of negotiable instruments (Article 11): Only bearer-name promissory notes may be issued, each not exceeding the installment amount and issued separately per installment; non-compliant notes are void against the consumer.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: The text covers the Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation (published in Official Gazette No. 29363, May 22, 2015). It includes: (1) Final provisions on entry into force and execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade; (2) Purpose, scope, legal basis (Law No. 6502, Articles 31 and 84), and comprehensive definitions (contractual/effective annual interest rates, fixed/indefinite-term contracts, early repayment, late interest, credit intermediary, credit provider, overdraft accounts, total cost of credit, payment plan, consumer, fees, etc.); (3) Scope exclusions (housing finance, 30-day overdrafts) and special rules for credit cards, installment cash advances, and participation banks; (4) Pre-contractual information obligations: format requirements (12-point font, clear language), detailed information lists for fixed-term and indefinite-term credit contracts (credit type, provider details, interest rates, total cost, payment plans, late interest, default consequences, insurance, guarantees, withdrawal rights, early repayment, rejection notification, binding period), exemption for auxiliary credit intermediaries, and mandatory immediate free written notification of credit application rejection.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
Sözleşmenin Şekli ve Zorunlu İçeriği
Sözleşmenin şekli
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of the Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation, addressing the form and mandatory content of contracts. Article 10 requires consumer credit contracts (except distance contracts) to be in writing, in at least 12-point font, clear and readable language, with a copy provided to the consumer. Article 11 specifies mandatory content for fixed-term credit contracts, including: credit type, parties' details, duration, total amount, fees, interest rates (contractual and effective annual), payment schedule, free copy right, account conditions, notary costs, late interest, default consequences, guarantees/suretyship rules, withdrawal rights, early repayment rights, dispute resolution options, foreign currency exchange rate rules, holiday installment adjustments, and prohibition of compound interest. It also addresses additional requirements for restructuring contracts due to default. Article 12 outlines mandatory content for indefinite-term credit contracts, covering credit type, parties' details, credit limit notification, interest rates, fees, termination conditions, late interest, default consequences, guarantees, withdrawal rights, dispute resolution, free copy right, and holiday payment adjustments.

nodes.title: Sözleşmede değişiklik yapılması
nodes.summary: The text covers two main provisions from a Turkish consumer credit regulation. Article 13 addresses contract modifications: fixed-term credit terms cannot be changed to the consumer's detriment; for indefinite-term contracts, changes to the contractual interest rate or other terms require 30 days' prior written notice (via paper or permanent data storage). Interest rate increases cannot be applied retroactively, and consumers can avoid the increase by repaying the full debt within 60 days of notification. Consumers may also exercise termination rights under Article 25 for other term changes. Article 14 governs the Effective Annual Interest Rate (EFYF): it must be stated in all consumer credit contracts, calculated per the Annex-1 formula, excluding fees from consumer non-compliance. The calculation assumes the contract runs for its full agreed duration with parties meeting obligations on time. Uncertain fees or variable interest rates are treated as fixed until contract end. Additional Annex-1 assumptions may be applied as needed.

nodes.title: Erken ödeme
nodes.summary: Article 15 on Early Payment: (1) Consumers may pay one or more installments before their due date or settle all/part of the credit debt early; the lender is obligated to apply the necessary discount, including cases where interest was collected upfront per Articles 16-17. (2) The early payment discount is calculated based on the date the consumer actually makes the payment, and this date cannot be altered to the consumer's detriment. (3) For credits where all or part of the interest was collected upfront, the lender must establish a system to apply the required discount at the contractual interest rate upon early payment, in accordance with Annex-3 provisions.

nodes.title: Kredinin tamamının erken ödenmesi
nodes.summary: Article 16 of the Consumer Credit Agreement Regulation outlines the rules for full early repayment of a loan. It specifies three scenarios: (1) If repayment occurs on an installment date, the due installment, remaining principal, and any uncollected interest, taxes, fees, and legal obligations are collected. (2) If repayment occurs between installments, accrued interest on principal since the last paid installment, remaining principal in future installments, and uncollected interest/taxes/fees are collected. In cases where interest was prepaid, a refund is calculated based on the early repayment date and amount using the contractual interest rate. (3) All full early repayment procedures must comply with the provisions set forth in Annex-2 of the regulation.

nodes.title: Ara ödeme
nodes.summary: Article 17 defines interim (pre)payment as any consumer payment of at least one installment amount before its due date. It specifies that upon prepayment, interest (calculated on remaining principal at the contractual rate from the prior installment date) plus applicable taxes and fees are collected; the remainder reduces the principal. A new payment plan is generated with unchanged installment count and dates, unless the consumer requests in writing and both parties agree to alter the number of installments or dates. With mutual consent, the new installment amount may exceed the pre-prepayment amount. For credits with upfront interest collection, a proportional interest refund is made based on the payment date and amount. The new payment plan must be provided in writing or via permanent data storage without any fee. The burden of proof regarding consumer requests rests with the creditor. Interim payment procedures must comply with Annex-4 provisions.

nodes.title: Temerrüt ve geç ödeme
nodes.summary: Article 18 covers default and late payment rules in consumer credit contracts. Paragraph 1: A lender may demand full repayment only if it has fulfilled all obligations and the consumer has defaulted on at least two consecutive installments, with a mandatory 30-day notice; interest and fees are excluded from calculating defaulted installments. Paragraph 2: Late interest cannot exceed the contractual rate plus 30%; any excess collected must be refunded with interest calculated at that 30%-above-contractual rate for the period between collection and refund. Paragraph 3: The lender may charge late interest on the principal of the late payment, based on the late interest rate and days overdue, plus applicable taxes and fees on that interest. The consumer's actual payment date is the reference for calculation, and this period cannot be altered to the consumer's detriment. Annex-5 provisions govern late interest calculations.

This section covers the form and mandatory content of consumer credit contracts under Turkish regulation. It specifies that contracts must be in writing, in at least 12-point font, with clear language and a copy provided to the consumer. It details mandatory content for both fixed-term and indefinite-term credit contracts, including credit type, parties' details, interest rates, fees, payment schedules, withdrawal rights, early repayment rights, dispute resolution, and default consequences. The section addresses contract modification rules, prohibiting detrimental changes to fixed-term contracts and requiring 30-day notice for indefinite-term changes, along with Effective Annual Interest Rate calculation requirements. It further covers early payment rights and discount calculations, full early repayment procedures under three scenarios, interim prepayment rules including new payment plan generation, and default/late payment provisions, including conditions for demanding full repayment, late interest caps (contractual rate plus 30%), and calculation methods.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
Bağlı kredi sözleşmesi
nodes.summary: Article 19 of Chapter 5 defines a linked credit agreement as consumer credit exclusively financing a specific goods/service contract, forming an objective economic unity. Economic unity is established if at least one condition is met: the seller finances the credit, the lender uses the seller's services in preparing the credit agreement, or the specific goods/service is explicitly stated in the credit contract. If the consumer withdraws from the goods/service contract and notifies the lender within the withdrawal period, the linked credit terminates without compensation or penalty. If goods/services are not delivered or performed properly, the consumer may withdraw or reduce the price; the seller, provider, and lender are jointly liable. Price reduction proportionally reduces the linked credit and adjusts the payment plan. The lender's liability for refund is limited to one year from the delivery/performance date and capped at the credit amount used. Credits where the lender pays for consumer-chosen goods without a specific seller-lender contract are excluded from linked credit classification.

nodes.title: Taksitli nakit avans kredisi
nodes.summary: The text covers three articles from Turkey's Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation. Article 20 defines installment cash advance credit (repayment in installments via credit card or overdraft accounts), requiring prior disclosure of total amount, installments, and interest rate; specifies interest calculation based on days elapsed; limits late interest to principal only; and restricts changing the account closing date until debt is settled. Article 21 addresses limit exceedance, mandating that contracts include interest rate information provided monthly in writing; requiring immediate written notification if exceedance exceeds one month (detailing amount, rate, and overdue interest); and allowing lenders to offer alternative credit contracts for prolonged exceedance. Article 22 governs interest rates: fixed-term credits have irrevocable fixed rates; missing rate information renders credit interest-free; only one contractual rate applies; compound interest is prohibited in all consumer transactions including default; and credit card interest cannot exceed the rate set in the card agreement.

nodes.title: Consumer Credit: Installment Credits, Limit Excess, and Interest Rates
nodes.summary: This page covers Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation provisions on installment cash advance credits, limit excess (Article 21), and interest rates (Article 22). For installment credits, it mandates prior disclosure of total amount, installments, and rates; specifies installment calculation by days elapsed; requires late interest from the due date; mandates separate principal/interest tracking with late interest on principal only; and restricts changing account closing dates. Article 21 requires overdraft-permitted deposit contracts to include contractual rate and conditions with monthly written notifications; immediate notice for significant excess over one month (amount, rate, late interest); and permits offering alternative credit. Article 22 establishes fixed rates for definite-term credits that cannot be changed against consumers; missing rate info renders credit interest-free; only one contractual rate is permitted; compound interest is prohibited; and credit card interest cannot exceed the contractual rate.

nodes.title: Hesap özeti
nodes.summary: Article 23 of the regulations covers account statement requirements for credit agreements. For indefinite-term credit agreements, lenders must provide consumers with a written or permanent-data-storage account statement at the end of each accounting period, including: the relevant period, credit amount and usage dates, next statement date, period debt, consumer payment dates and amounts, contractual interest rate, late payment interest rate, fees collected, and minimum payment amount if applicable. For definite-term credit agreements, the payment plan provided at contract formation serves as the account statement, provided it includes: required payments, installment periods and conditions, principal amount of each repayment, and a breakdown of interest calculated at the contractual rate along with any additional fees.

nodes.title: Cayma hakkı
nodes.summary: The text covers Articles 24-28 of the Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation. Article 24 details the consumer's 14-day right of withdrawal without reason or penalty, including start date rules, lender's burden of proof, repayment obligations (principal plus contractual interest within 30 days), prohibition on additional fees, and termination of linked service contracts. Article 25 addresses termination of indefinite-term credit contracts: consumers may terminate without fee (max 1-month notice if specified), lenders require 2-month notice, and just-cause termination without notice is permitted if agreed. Article 26 prohibits imposing insurance without the consumer's explicit written request, allows consumer-chosen insurers, requires insurance to match credit terms, and mandates insurance termination upon early repayment or restructuring unless the consumer consents. Article 27 states that when a lender transfers contractual rights to a third party, the consumer may assert rights against that party, and written notification to the consumer is mandatory. Article 28 classifies personal guarantees taken from consumers as simple guarantees and those given by counterparties as joint and several guarantees.

nodes.title: Consumer Credit: Termination, Insurance, Rights Transfer, and Guarantees
nodes.summary: The page covers Articles 25–28 of the Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation. Article 25 addresses termination of indefinite credit contracts: consumers may terminate without fee (notice max 1 month), lenders need 2 months' notice or just cause with written notification. Article 26 prohibits imposing insurance without the consumer's explicit written request; consumers may choose their insurer, and amount insurance must match remaining debt and term; early repayment ends insurance unless the consumer consents to continuation. Article 27 states that when a lender transfers contractual rights to a third party, the consumer may assert their rights against that party, and written notification to the consumer is mandatory. Article 28 classifies personal guarantees taken from consumers as simple guarantees, while guarantees given to consumers as joint and several guarantees.

nodes.title: Other Provisions, Repealed Regulation, and Entry into Force
nodes.summary: Article 29 (Other Matters) stipulates that no fees may be charged for accounts opened solely for fixed-term credit contracts, which close upon credit repayment unless the consumer requests otherwise. A credit deposit account cannot be created without the consumer's explicit instruction. All fee information must be provided in writing as a contract annex, with the burden of proof on the credit provider. Installment due dates falling on legal holidays automatically shift to the next non-holiday day. Any dedicated phone line provided by the credit provider must not exceed standard tariff rates. Article 30 repeals the 2003 Regulation on Early Payment Discount and Annual Cost Rate Calculation Procedures. Article 31 states the regulation enters into force six months after its publication date.

nodes.title: Yürütme
nodes.summary: The text contains the execution clause (Article 32) of a Turkish regulation, stating that the Minister of Customs and Trade is responsible for implementing its provisions. It also includes repeated page headers and footers (pages 70–82) from the Consumer Credit Agreements Regulation (Tüketici Kredisi Sözleşmeleri Yönetmeliği) and the Regulations (Yönetmelikler) section. Finally, it references the Housing Finance Agreements Regulation (Konut Finansmanı Sözleşmeleri Yönetmeliği), published in the Official Gazette (Resmî Gazete) on May 28, 2015, issue number 29369.

This section (Fifth Chapter: Various and Final Provisions) of Turkey's Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation covers: linked credit agreements (definition, economic unity conditions, withdrawal, joint liability, price reduction, lender liability limits); installment cash advance credits (disclosure, interest calculation, late interest limits); limit exceedance procedures (notifications, alternative credit offers); interest rate rules (fixed rates, no compound interest, single rate requirement); account statement requirements for indefinite and definite-term credits; the consumer's 14-day right of withdrawal; termination of indefinite-term credits (notice periods, just cause); insurance restrictions (no forced insurance, consumer choice); rights transfer to third parties; classification of guarantees (simple vs. joint and several); other provisions (no fees for credit-only accounts, fee disclosure, holiday adjustments, phone line rates); repeal of the 2003 Early Payment Discount Regulation; entry into force six months after publication; and execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade.

nodes.title: KONUT FİNANSMANI SÖZLEŞMELERİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of the Housing Finance Contracts Regulation, covering: (1) Purpose – establishing procedures and principles for housing finance contracts; (2) Scope – applying to housing finance contracts, treating housing cooperative members as consumers, and applying to participation banks with profit-share considerations; (3) Legal Basis – grounded in Articles 39 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502; and (4) Definitions – defining key terms including contractual interest rate, current interest rate, variable interest, early payment, financial leasing contract, late payment interest rate, permanent data storage, housing finance institution, housing finance contract, total cost of credit, payment plan, installment, installment due date, consumer, fee, and annual cost rate.

This section covers three regulatory areas under Turkish consumer credit law. First, it details the form and mandatory content of consumer credit contracts, including writing requirements, font specifications, required clauses for fixed and indefinite-term contracts, modification rules, early repayment rights and discount calculations, and default/late payment provisions with interest caps. Second, it addresses various and final provisions of the Consumer Credit Contracts Regulation, encompassing linked credit agreements, installment cash advances, limit exceedance procedures, interest rate rules, account statement requirements, the 14-day withdrawal right, termination of indefinite-term credits, insurance restrictions, rights transfer, guarantee classification, fee disclosures, repeal of the 2003 Early Payment Discount Regulation, and entry-into-force provisions. Third, it presents the first chapter of the Housing Finance Contracts Regulation, defining its purpose, scope (including housing cooperatives and participation banks), legal basis under Consumer Protection Law No. 6502, and key terminology such as contractual interest rate, total cost of credit, payment plan, and housing finance institution.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 of the Housing Finance Agreements Regulation, detailing pre-contractual information obligations. Article 5 specifies the format requirements for the pre-contractual information form (minimum 12-point font, clear language, provided on paper or durable medium). Article 6 enumerates the mandatory content of the form, including: interest rate type, institution identification details, contract duration, total credit amount and fees, debt distribution breakdown, appraisal requirements, account conditions, late payment interest, guarantee/surety information, insurance restrictions, rejection notification, transfer conditions, binding period, and definitions of fixed/variable interest. It further details specific disclosures for fixed-rate loans (rates, installments, early repayment rights, sample payment plans) and variable-rate loans (reference indices, margins, maximum rates, payment plans). Article 7 mandates that housing finance institutions must immediately and free of charge inform consumers in writing or via durable medium when a credit application is rejected.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of the Housing Finance Contracts Regulation, addressing the contract's form and mandatory content. Article 8 stipulates that housing finance contracts must be in writing to be valid, prohibits institutions from later invoking invalidity to the consumer's detriment, and requires contracts to be in at least 12-point font, clear, readable language, with a copy provided on paper or permanent storage. Article 9 lists mandatory contract content: consumer's personal and contact details, payment schedule, loan conditions, property information, consumer rights (if structured as a loan), automatic postponement of installment due dates falling on holidays, prohibition of compound interest including in default, foreign currency exchange rate reference date, consumer's right to file disputes at consumer courts or arbitration boards, the right to a free contract copy in the first year, and other available dispute resolution channels. It also requires that financial leasing contracts for housing finance include equivalent information with appropriate wording.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
Tarafların Hak ve Yükümlülükleri
Sigorta yaptırılması
nodes.summary: This text is from the Fourth Chapter (Rights and Obligations of the Parties) of a housing finance regulation, specifically Article 10 on insurance. It states that: (1) Insurance cannot be imposed on the consumer without their explicit written or permanent-data-storage request. (2) The consumer may choose any insurance company, and the housing finance institution must accept the coverage. (3) The insurance must align with the loan's subject, remaining debt amount, and maturity. (4) In amount insurance, the coverage cannot exceed the remaining loan balance, and the insurance term cannot exceed the loan term. (5) Mandatory earthquake insurance provisions remain applicable. (6) In loan-linked amount insurance, early repayment or changes to the loan structure terminate the insurance contract. (7) However, with the consumer's explicit approval and notification, the policy may continue under existing terms or be adjusted in coverage amount and duration to match the modified loan structure.

nodes.title: Erken ödeme
nodes.summary: Article 11 governs early payment in housing finance contracts. Consumers may prepay the full amount or any sum not less than one installment. The institution must apply appropriate deductions. Interest is calculated on remaining principal using the applicable rate (fixed, current, or mixed) from the last installment date, plus taxes/fees; the remainder reduces principal. A new payment plan is generated with unchanged installment count and dates, unless the consumer requests a payment-free period or mutually agreed different terms. The burden of proof for consumer requests lies with the institution. The new plan must be provided free of charge in writing or via permanent data storage. For fixed-rate contracts, early payment compensation may be charged (max 1% if remaining term ≤36 months, max 2% if >36 months), capped at the total deduction; no compensation applies for variable rates. The payment date is the reference date and cannot be altered to the consumer's detriment. Annex-2 and Annex-3 provisions apply, including mandatory systems for upfront-interest loans.

nodes.title: Yeniden finansman
nodes.summary: Article 12 of the Housing Finance Contracts Regulation defines refinancing as occurring when, by mutual agreement between the housing finance institution and the consumer, at least one of the following changes is made to the contract: (a) modification of the credit interest rate, (b) change in the credit term/maturity, (c) change in the type of interest, (d) consolidation of multiple housing finance contracts secured by the same property into a single contract, or (e) change in the credit currency. The article further stipulates that consumer consent must be obtained in writing or via a permanent data storage medium before any refinancing changes are made. Prior to obtaining consent, the institution is required to provide the consumer with comparative information detailing the proposed changes, presented in at least 12-point font, in clear, simple, and readable language, on paper or through a permanent data storage medium.

nodes.title: Temerrüt ve geç ödeme
nodes.summary: Article 13 covers default and late payment rules in housing finance contracts. It specifies conditions for demanding full repayment upon consumer default (institution must have fulfilled obligations, consumer must miss at least two consecutive installments, and 30 days' notice is required). Interest and fees are excluded from accelerated installment calculations. Late payment interest is capped at 30% above the contractual (fixed) or current (variable) rate, with mandatory refund of excess amounts plus interest. The institution may charge late interest on principal based on days overdue, using the consumer's payment date as reference. In financial leasing, if the consumer fails to perform within the notice period, the institution may terminate the contract and must immediately sell the property after obtaining an appraisal, notifying the consumer at least 10 business days before sale. Any surplus after debt repayment is returned to the consumer. Post-sale, the consumer or third-party possessor must vacate the property, or enforcement proceedings under Law 2004 may be initiated. Late interest calculations follow Annex-4.

This section outlines the rights and obligations of parties in housing finance contracts, covering four key areas: (1) Insurance: consumers must explicitly consent to insurance, may choose any insurer, coverage must align with the loan, and mandatory earthquake insurance applies; early repayment or loan restructuring terminates or adjusts the policy. (2) Early payment: consumers may prepay any amount of at least one installment; interest is recalculated on remaining principal, a new payment plan is generated free of charge, and fixed-rate contracts may incur compensation (up to 1–2% depending on remaining term). (3) Refinancing: defined as mutual agreement to modify interest rate, term, interest type, consolidate contracts, or change currency; requires written consumer consent preceded by clear comparative information in at least 12-point font. (4) Default and late payment: full repayment may be demanded after two missed installments with 30 days' notice; late interest is capped at 30% above the contractual rate; in financial leasing, the institution may terminate and sell the property after appraisal, returning any surplus to the consumer.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 5 (Various and Final Provisions) of the Housing Finance Contracts Regulation. Article 14 defines interest in credits and financial leasing, rules for fixed/variable rates, CBTC reference indices, consumer information duties, prohibition of compound interest, and written notification for rate changes. Article 15 defines linked credit contracts, economic unity criteria, joint liability of seller and finance institution for non-delivery (limited to one year and credit amount), liability continuity upon credit transfer, and exclusions. title: Ek – 2
summary: This text is Appendix 2 of the Housing Finance Contract Regulations, detailing rules and examples for early repayment of a credit (full or partial, minimum one installment). Each example demonstrates accrued interest collection, principal deduction, penalty calculation, and recalculation of remaining installments.

nodes.title: Örnek 1:
nodes.summary: This text presents Example 1 from the Housing Finance Contracts Regulation, illustrating the step-by-step processing of a consumer's early payment of 13,750 TL on the 20th installment (dated 20.08.2016). nodes.title: Örnek 2:

nodes.summary: This text is the Turkish Regulation on Prepaid Housing Sales (Official Gazette, Nov 27, 2014, No. 29188), based on Consumer Protection Law No. 6502. It covers: (1) Purpose, scope, and legal basis; (2) Definitions of key terms including linked credit contract, housing, housing finance institution, prepayment amount, prepaid housing sales contract, seller, and consumer; (3) Mandatory pre-information form requirements (at least 1 day before contract, 12-point font, including seller/property details, prices, interest, withdrawal rights, delivery date, guarantee, building permit date, and common expenses), plus supplementary plans and building completion insurance form; (4) Form requirements: contract must be written with co-ownership transfer registration or notarized sale promise, no payment before valid contract, and building permit is mandatory; (5) Mandatory contract content listing 15 items covering parties, property details, pricing, interest, default consequences, payment plan, withdrawal/termination rights, guarantee, delivery, and dispute resolution provisions.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
key_items: Cayma ve Sözleşmeden Dönme Hakkının Kullanımı
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 3 of Turkey's Regulation on Pre-paid Housing Sales, covering two main consumer rights. Article 8 (Right of Withdrawal): Consumers may withdraw within 14 days without reason or penalty; notification via notary suffices. If linked credit is used, the seller must inform the finance institution, which cannot charge fees during the withdrawal period. Building completion insurance and credit agreements take effect only after the withdrawal period. Refunds and debt documents must be returned within 14 days; consumers return the property within 10 days. The seller bears the burden of proving the consumer was informed. Article 9 (Contract Termination): Consumers may terminate within 24 months without reason. The seller may claim tiered compensation (2% to 8% depending on elapsed time) plus taxes/fees. However, no compensation is owed if the seller fails obligations, the consumer dies, loses income, or if the housing is sold to multiple consumers. Refunds are due within 180 days; with linked credit, the finance institution refunds the consumer after deducting compensation. Consumers return the property within 10 days of receiving the refund.

nodes.summary: This text covers Chapters 4-6 of Turkey's Pre-Paid Housing Sales Regulation. Chapter 4 (Seller's Other Obligations) sets a 36-month maximum delivery period, defines delivery conditions, and requires written notification of project changes, allowing consumers to cancel within one month without fees (with limited deductions for legal/force majeure changes). Chapter 5 (Guarantee Principles) mandates that projects with 30+ units secure consumer payments via building completion insurance, bank guarantee letter, progress payment system, or linked credit. It details each mechanism: insurance compensation is protected from seizure; bank guarantees must be definitive and unlimited; progress payments are held in blocked accounts released only against verified construction progress with no bank commissions; linked credit covers the loan amount with separate guarantees for excess. Chapter 6 (Final Provisions) repeals the 2003 promotional sales regulation, applies a transitional rule (contracts governed by regulations in effect at signing), states the regulation enters force upon publication, and assigns enforcement to the Minister of Customs and Trade. Published in Official Gazette 27/11/2014, amended 11/3/2017.
