nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Regulation on Contracts Concluded Outside Business Premises (published in the Official Gazette, January 14, 2015). It covers: (1) Purpose – regulating procedures for off-premises contracts and direct sales; (2) Scope – applicability to such contracts, with exclusions for financial services, real estate transactions, housing rental, package tours, timeshare, fairs/markets, regular food/beverage deliveries, sales under 30 TL, installation/maintenance, electronic communication services, and utility subscriptions; (3) Legal basis – Articles 47 and 84 of Consumer Protection Law No. 6502; (4) Definitions – defining key terms including ministry, service, provincial directorate, business premises, off-premises contracts (three types: simultaneous physical presence, immediate follow-up after off-premises meeting, and during organized trips), permanent data storage, goods, provider, seller, consumer, remote communication means, ancillary contract, and authorization certificate.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 2 of the Turkish Regulation on Contracts Concluded Outside Business Premises, covering three articles. Article 5 (Pre-contractual Information) requires sellers to inform consumers in writing (min. 12-point font, clear language) about goods/services characteristics, seller identity, total price in TL, and withdrawal conditions before binding them; the burden of proof lies with the seller. Article 6 (Form and Validity) mandates that such contracts be made by authorized sellers, be in writing, formatted in at least 12-point readable font, with a copy given to the consumer; sellers cannot later invoke invalidity to the consumer's detriment. Article 7 (Mandatory Contract Content) lists eleven required elements including parties' identities, contact details, price, dates, payment info, withdrawal conditions and notification address, cases where withdrawal is unavailable, a mandatory 14-day withdrawal statement (which must appear on page one in 16-point bold), bank details, and consumer court/arbitration information. Consumers must sign and handwrite specific acknowledgment statements.

nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of Turkey's Off-Premises Contracts Regulation, detailing the consumer's right of withdrawal (Articles 8-14). Key points include: the 14-day withdrawal period without reason or penalty, with specific start dates depending on whether the contract involves goods delivery or service; rules for multiple items, parts, and regular deliveries; the seller's obligation to prove proper information was provided, with a one-year maximum extension if not; the method of exercising withdrawal (written notice or form) and the consumer's burden of proof; the seller's prohibition on demanding payment during the withdrawal period and obligation to collect goods within 14 days; the consumer's exemption from liability for normal-use deterioration; automatic termination of ancillary contracts upon withdrawal with no penalties; and exceptions to the withdrawal right, including personalized goods, perishables, hygiene-sensitive opened items, digital content, and services commenced with consumer consent.

nodes.title: Satıcı veya Sağlayıcının Diğer Yükümlülükleri
nodes.summary: The text outlines seller/provider obligations under a consumer protection regulation, covering four articles: (1) Contract performance (Art. 15): the seller must deliver goods/services within the committed timeframe, cannot charge extra delivery/shipping fees if delivery is scheduled after contract formation, and bears responsibility for loss or damage until delivery to the consumer or a designated third party. (2) Burden of proof (Art. 16): the seller/provider must prove that the contract was delivered to the consumer and that the goods/services were provided. (3) Phone usage fees (Art. 17): if a dedicated phone line is allocated for consumer contact, the seller cannot apply a rate higher than the standard tariff. (4) Information retention (Art. 18): the seller/provider is required to retain all records and documents related to the contract, withdrawal rights, information obligations, delivery, and other duties for a period of three years.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM Yetki Belgesi
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter Five (Authorization Certificate) of a Turkish regulation. It outlines: (1) the obligation for sellers/providers to obtain an authorization certificate from the provincial directorate where their headquarters is located (Art. 19); (2) application requirements, including two authorization certificates, trade registry, notary-approved signature circulars, chamber activity certificate, tax certificate, audited financial statements, list of goods/services, consumer cancellation address, and payment account details, with a 15-day deadline to report any changes (Art. 20); (3) evaluation criteria, where the provincial directorate considers ministry inspections and consumer complaints (Art. 21); (4) a two-year validity period with reapplication required upon expiry (Art. 22); and (5) certificate cancellation if violations persist 30 days after a warning, a one-year reissuance ban, and public announcement on the ministry website (Art. 23).

nodes.title: ALTINCI BÖLÜM Doğrudan Satış Sistemi
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 6 of the Off-Premises Contracts Regulation, defining the Direct Sales System. Article 24 defines direct sales as selling goods/services outside retail locations (e.g., consumer's home or workplace) by representatives, distributors, or similar roles, using single or multi-tier methods, and defines direct sales companies and direct sellers. Article 25 establishes fundamental principles: the system must prioritize selling goods/services over recruiting; earnings cannot be based primarily on recruitment-based commissions or bonuses; misleading information, pressure, or deception are prohibited; no entry fees, starter packages, or renewal charges may be collected from direct sellers; sellers may leave without penalty, and if within 60 days, the company must repurchase unused goods and refund within 14 days; both companies and sellers must comply with the regulation; only the company needs a license; additional disclosure requirements apply; the company bears responsibility for Article 18 obligations; minors, legally incapacitated persons, and company insiders cannot be direct sellers; and the company is jointly and severally liable for all direct sales activities.

This section of Turkey's Off-Premises Contracts Regulation covers: (1) the consumer's 14-day right of withdrawal, including start dates, methods, seller obligations to collect goods, consumer exemptions, ancillary contract termination, and exceptions (personalized, perishable, hygiene-sensitive, digital content, commenced services); (2) seller/provider obligations regarding timely delivery, burden of proof, phone tariff limits, and three-year record retention; (3) the authorization certificate system, including application requirements, evaluation criteria, two-year validity, and cancellation procedures; (4) the Direct Sales System, defining it, establishing principles prohibiting recruitment-based earnings, entry fees, and misleading practices, while granting sellers exit rights and imposing joint liability on companies; and (5) final provisions repealing the 2003 door-to-door sales regulation, setting a transitional deadline, entry into force, and designating the Minister of Customs and Trade as the executing authority.

nodes.title: Distance Contracts Regulation: Purpose, Scope, and Legal Basis
nodes.summary: This page from the Official Gazette (Nov 27, 2014, Issue 29188) presents the first chapter of the Distance Contracts Regulation. Article 1 states the purpose is to regulate procedures and principles governing distance contracts. Article 2 defines the scope, applying to distance contracts while excluding: financial services, automatic machine sales, public phone telecom use, gambling/lottery services, real estate transactions, housing rental, package tours, timeshare arrangements, regular delivery of daily consumables, passenger transport (with certain information obligations preserved), installation/maintenance/repair, and social services such as nursing and care. Article 3 establishes the legal basis as Articles 48 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502, dated Nov 7, 2013).

nodes.title: Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is Article 4 (Definitions) of the Distance Contracts Regulation, defining key terms used throughout the regulation. It defines: digital content (programs, apps, games, music, video, text); service (consumer transactions other than goods provision for a fee); permanent data storage (SMS, email, internet, disk, CD, DVD, memory card, etc.); the Law (Law No. 6502 on Consumer Protection); goods (movable property, residential/vacation real estate, and intangible goods like software, audio, video); distance contract (contracts formed without simultaneous physical presence using remote communication tools); provider (entities offering services commercially); seller (entities offering goods commercially); consumer (individuals acting for non-commercial purposes); remote communication tool (mail, catalog, phone, fax, radio, TV, email, SMS, internet); and ancillary contract (additional goods/services related to a distance contract provided by seller, provider, or a third party).

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 (Pre-Information Obligation) of the Distance Contracts Regulation. Article 5 details the mandatory pre-contractual information sellers must provide consumers, including product characteristics, seller identity and contact details, total price with taxes and extra costs, payment/delivery terms, withdrawal rights and conditions, deposits, digital content compatibility, and dispute resolution options. It establishes that this information is integral to the contract, specifies pricing rules for subscriptions, allows exceptions for auctions, and places the burden of proof on the seller. Article 6 prescribes the method of delivery: information must be in at least 12-point font, clear and readable, with specific requirements for internet-based contracts (displaying key info before payment), voice communication (verbal disclosure before order plus written follow-up), limited-space environments, and instant service sales. Article 7 requires sellers to obtain consumer confirmation of receiving pre-information, otherwise the contract is void. Article 8 mandates informing consumers that placing an order constitutes a payment obligation and requires sellers to identify themselves and the commercial purpose when calling consumers for distance contracts.

nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 on the consumer's right of withdrawal and parties' obligations. Article 9 defines the 14-day withdrawal right without reason or penalty, specifying when the period starts (contract date for services, delivery date for goods), special rules for multiple items, parts, and regular deliveries, and clarifies that carrier delivery does not equal consumer delivery. Article 10 addresses insufficient information: the seller must prove the consumer was informed; if not, the 14-day limit is lifted but expires one year after the withdrawal period ends. Article 11 outlines how to exercise withdrawal (written notice, form, or clear declaration before the deadline), online options with mandatory confirmation, phone-sale form requirements, and places the burden of proof on the consumer. Article 12 mandates the seller to refund all payments, including delivery costs, within 14 days of receiving the withdrawal notice, using the original payment method without additional cost to the consumer.

nodes.title: Consumer Withdrawal Rights: Period, Information, and Usage
nodes.summary: The text covers regulations on the consumer's right of withdrawal (cayma hakkı). It specifies how the withdrawal period is determined for single orders, multi-part goods, and regular delivery contracts, noting that delivery to a carrier does not count as consumer delivery, and that goods-delivery rules apply in combined goods-services contracts. Article 10 (Eksik bilgilendirme) states the seller must prove the consumer was informed about withdrawal rights; if not properly informed, the 14-day period does not apply but expires one year after the withdrawal period ends, and if information is provided within that year, the 14-day period starts from that date. Article 11 (Cayma hakkının kullanımı) requires written or permanent-data notification before the deadline, allows use of a standard form or clear declaration, permits website-based submission with immediate confirmation, mandates form delivery for phone sales by the delivery date, and places the burden of proof on the consumer.

nodes.title: Satıcı veya sağlayıcının yükümlülükleri
nodes.summary: Article 12 of the Distance Contracts Regulation outlines the seller/supplier's obligations upon a consumer's exercise of the right of withdrawal. Key points: (1) The seller must refund all collected payments, including delivery costs, within 14 days of receiving the withdrawal notice. (2) Refunds must be made in a single transaction using the consumer's original payment method, without imposing any additional cost or obligation on the consumer. (3) Regarding return shipping: if the consumer uses the seller-designated carrier, the consumer bears no return costs; if no carrier was specified in advance, no return fee may be charged; and if the designated carrier lacks a branch in the consumer's area, the seller must arrange pickup at no extra cost to the consumer.

nodes.title: Tüketicinin yükümlülükleri
nodes.summary: The text covers consumer obligations related to the right of withdrawal in Turkish consumer law. Article 13 states that unless the seller/supplier offers to collect the goods, the consumer must return them within 10 days of the withdrawal notice to the seller or their authorized representative. It also clarifies that the consumer is not liable for changes or deterioration resulting from using the goods in accordance with their function, technical specifications, and usage instructions during the withdrawal period. Article 14 addresses the effect of withdrawal on ancillary contracts: upon exercise of the right of withdrawal, ancillary contracts terminate automatically (subject to Article 30 of the law), and the consumer is not required to pay any costs, compensation, or penalties except in cases specified in Article 13(2). Additionally, the seller/supplier must immediately notify the third party involved in the ancillary contract about the consumer's withdrawal.

nodes.title: Cayma hakkının istisnaları
nodes.summary: Article 15 of the regulation lists exceptions to the consumer's right of withdrawal. Unless otherwise agreed, consumers cannot withdraw from contracts involving: (a) goods/services with prices tied to financial market fluctuations; (b) goods made to personal specifications; (c) perishable or expiring goods; (ç) goods with opened protective packaging unsuitable for return due to health/hygiene; (d) goods that irreversibly mix with other products; (e) physical books, digital content, and computer consumables with opened packaging; (f) periodicals (newspapers/magazines) outside subscriptions; (g) date-specific services (accommodation, transport, car rental, food/beverage, leisure); (ğ) instantly performed electronic services or instantly delivered intangible goods; and (h) services commenced with consumer consent before the withdrawal period expires.

This section covers the consumer's right of withdrawal in distance contracts and both parties' obligations. It defines the 14-day withdrawal period, its commencement for goods and services, and rules for multi-part or regular deliveries. It addresses insufficient information scenarios where the seller must prove the consumer was informed, otherwise the period extends up to one year. The section outlines how to exercise withdrawal (written notice, standard form, online submission) with the burden of proof on the consumer. Seller obligations include refunding all payments including delivery costs within 14 days via the original payment method, and return shipping arrangements. Consumer obligations include returning goods within 10 days and exemption from liability for normal-use deterioration. The automatic termination of ancillary contracts upon withdrawal is specified. Finally, exceptions to the withdrawal right are listed, covering personalized goods, perishables, hygiene-sensitive items, opened digital content, date-specific services, and other categories.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Diğer Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers Articles 16-23 and an appendix of Turkey's Distance Contracts Regulation. Article 16 addresses contract performance and delivery timelines (max 30 days for goods), consumer's right to terminate, refund obligations within 14 days with legal interest, and procedures when performance becomes impossible. Article 17 defines seller liability for loss/damage until delivery, with exceptions when consumer selects a different carrier. Article 18 prohibits above-standard phone rates for contract-related communication. Article 19 requires explicit consumer consent for additional charges and mandates immediate refunds for auto-selected options. Article 20 imposes 3-year document retention on sellers and intermediaries, with an exception for public service platforms, and requires sellers to prove defect-free delivery of intangible goods/services. Articles 21-23 repeal the 2011 regulation, set a 3-month entry-into-force period, and assign execution to the Minister of Customs and Trade. The appendix provides a sample cancellation form with fields for seller details, order information, goods/services description, price, and consumer identification.

This section of Turkey's Distance Contracts Regulation covers the consumer's right of withdrawal and other provisions. It details the 14-day withdrawal period, its commencement for goods and services, multi-part delivery rules, and extended periods when sellers fail to provide information. It specifies how to exercise withdrawal (written notice, standard form, online), seller refund obligations (including delivery costs within 14 days), consumer return duties (10 days), ancillary contract termination, and exceptions (personalized goods, perishables, hygiene items, opened digital content, date-specific services). Additionally, it addresses contract performance timelines (30-day max delivery), seller liability for loss/damage until delivery, prohibitions on above-standard phone rates, explicit consent for additional charges, 3-year document retention, proof of defect-free delivery for intangible goods, repeal of the 2011 regulation, a 3-month entry-into-force period, execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade, and a sample cancellation form appendix.

nodes.title: FİNANSAL HİZMETLERE İLİŞKİN MESAFELİ SÖZLEŞMELER YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text is the First Chapter (Purpose, Scope, Legal Basis, and Definitions) of the Regulation on Distance Contracts for Financial Services, published in the Official Gazette on January 31, 2015 (Issue 29253). Article 1 states the purpose: regulating procedures and principles for distance contracts related to financial services. Article 2 defines the scope, specifying that the regulation applies to initial agreements and subsequent transactions, with specific rules when no initial agreement exists (Article 5 applies only to the first transaction; a new cycle begins after one year of inactivity). It excludes certain consumer credit contract provisions and excludes payments (other than banking, credit, insurance, individual pension, and investment-related) and housing finance contracts. Article 3 establishes the legal basis as Articles 49 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 (November 7, 2013). Article 4 provides definitions for: financial services, distance contracts for financial services, permanent data storage, the Law, provider, consumer, remote communication means, and ancillary contracts.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 of the Regulation on Distance Contracts for Financial Services, detailing pre-information obligations. Article 5 mandates providers to inform consumers before contract formation about: provider/intermediary identity and contact details, service characteristics, total price including taxes, special risks of financial instruments, additional fees, information validity period, payment/performance terms, remote communication costs, withdrawal right conditions and procedures, withdrawal notification contacts, cases where withdrawal is unavailable, minimum duration for recurring services, and unilateral termination/penalty terms. Article 6 specifies the method: information must be at least 12-point font, clear, and provided in writing or via permanent data storage; for voice/limited environments, only key items suffice (except consumer credit contracts requiring full disclosure); commercial purpose must be evident, and identity must be stated at the start of voice calls. Article 7 requires the contract to include consumer personal details, complaint/objection rights (consumer court/arbiter), guarantee fund info, other resolution paths, and payment plans, with timing rules and the consumer's right to request a free written copy and change communication method.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
Cayma Hakkının Kullanımı ve Tarafların Yükümlülükleri
Consumer Withdrawal Rights and Provider Obligations in Financial Services
nodes.summary: Article 8 grants consumers the right to withdraw from distance financial service contracts within 14 days without reason or penalty; insurance and individual pension contracts follow other consumer-favorable legislation. The withdrawal period starts from the contract date or from when all terms were delivered, whichever is later. The provider must prove the consumer was informed about withdrawal rights. Article 9 specifies that withdrawal can be exercised via written notice or permanent data storage, using the annex form or a clear declaration; providers may offer a website option and must immediately confirm receipt of online withdrawal requests. Article 10 obligates providers to refund all payments (except Article 11 costs) within 30 days via the original payment method, in a single transaction, without imposing any cost on the consumer. Consumer acceptance declarations must be recorded physically or electronically, and providers must take necessary measures for such records.

nodes.title: Consumer Cancellation Obligations, Ancillary Contract Effects, and Exceptions
nodes.summary: This page from the Regulation on Distance Contracts for Financial Services covers three areas. Article 11 (Consumer's Obligations): Upon cancellation, the consumer must return service fees, public institution charges, and mandatory payments within 30 days; failure voids the cancellation. The refundable amount is capped at the proportion of service rendered and cannot serve as a penalty. The provider must prove they informed the consumer of the calculation method to claim these amounts. Article 12 (Effect on Ancillary Contracts): Cancellation terminates any ancillary contract without compensation or penalty, and the provider must immediately notify the third party in writing or via permanent data storage. Article 13 (Exceptions to Cancellation Right): Cancellation is unavailable for contracts tied to market-fluctuating prices (forex, securities, futures, swaps, options, etc.), short-term insurance policies under one month, and contracts fully performed with the consumer's explicit prior consent.

nodes.title: Financial Services Distance Contract: Termination, Proof, Fees, and Effectiveness
nodes.summary: This page covers Articles 14–17 of a regulation on financial services distance contracts. Article 14 states that consumers may terminate contracts via any remote communication tool and cannot be required to use conditions heavier than those used to establish the contract. Article 15 assigns the burden of proof for consumer information to the provider, mandates three-year retention of documents related to withdrawal rights and information obligations, and requires intermediaries to maintain and disclose transaction records for three years. Article 16 prohibits providers from charging above the regular rate for phone lines allocated for consumer contact. Article 17 specifies that the regulation enters into force three months after its publication date.

nodes.title: Yürütme
nodes.summary: The text covers Article 18 of a regulation, stating that the Minister of Customs and Trade is responsible for executing its provisions. It also includes an appendix from the Regulation on Distance Contracts for Financial Services, presenting a sample cancellation (withdrawal) form. The form is to be completed and sent only when the consumer wishes to exercise the right of withdrawal. It contains fields for the provider's details (name, title, address, fax, email), the service subject to withdrawal, the execution date, and the consumer's information (full name, address, and signature, with the signature required only for paper submissions).

This section covers the use of the withdrawal right and parties' obligations in distance financial service contracts. It details the consumer's 14-day withdrawal right without reason or penalty, the methods for exercising it (written notice, permanent data storage, or website), and the provider's duty to confirm receipt and refund all payments within 30 days via the original method. Consumer obligations upon cancellation include returning service fees within 30 days, with refunds capped at the proportion of service rendered. Cancellation terminates ancillary contracts without penalty, and providers must notify third parties. Exceptions apply to market-fluctuating price contracts, short-term insurance, and fully performed contracts. The section also addresses termination via remote communication, the provider's burden of proof, three-year document retention, prohibition on above-regular phone rates, and the regulation's entry into force three months after publication. Execution is assigned to the Minister of Customs and Trade, and a sample cancellation form with provider and consumer fields is provided as an appendix.

nodes.title: DEVRE TATİL VE UZUN SÜRELİ TATİL HİZMETİ SÖZLEŞMELERİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 1 (Purpose, Scope, Legal Basis, and Definitions) of Turkey's Regulation on Timeshare and Long-term Holiday Service Contracts. It establishes the regulation's purpose: to set procedures for timeshare, long-term holiday service, exchange, and resale contracts. The scope covers all such contracts, clarifying that personal/real rights, association membership, or bundled travel services do not exclude applicability, and defines timeshare contracts as those exceeding one year with multiple accommodation periods. The legal basis is Articles 50 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502, 2013). The definitions section defines key terms including: Minister/Ministry (Customs and Trade), exchange contract, timeshare right, timeshare contract, permanent data storage, prepayment amount, pre-paid timeshare contract, total project cost, provider, seller, consumer, and resale contract.

This section covers two main topics. First, it details the withdrawal right in distance financial service contracts, including the consumer's 14-day penalty-free withdrawal, exercise methods, provider obligations (confirmation, 30-day refund), consumer duties upon cancellation, termination of ancillary contracts, applicable exceptions (market-fluctuating prices, short-term insurance, fully performed contracts), remote termination procedures, burden of proof, three-year document retention, phone rate restrictions, the regulation's entry into force, execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade, and a sample cancellation form. Second, it presents Chapter 1 of Turkey's Regulation on Timeshare and Long-term Holiday Service Contracts, establishing its purpose, scope (covering timeshare, long-term holiday, exchange, and resale contracts), legal basis (Articles 50 and 84 of Consumer Protection Law No. 6502), and definitions of key terms such as timeshare right, provider, consumer, prepayment amount, and resale contract.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 of a Turkish consumer protection regulation on pre-contractual information and contract obligations. Article 5 requires sellers/providers to deliver a pre-information form at least one day before contract formation, in writing or via permanent data storage, in at least 12-point readable font. The form must contain type-specific information (timeshare, long-term holiday, resale, exchange, prepaid timeshare) per designated annexes. Changes are permitted only in extraordinary unforeseeable cases with consumer consent. Promotional invitations (gift holidays, campaigns, free meals/tours) must be disclosed before advertising. The burden of proof for information provision lies with the seller. Article 6 mandates that contracts include pre-information details plus consumer identity, address, contact info, and signing place/date. Contracts must be provided in writing or via permanent data storage, in at least 12-point readable font. Except for distance sales, consumers must write the date in their own handwriting and sign. The seller bears the burden of proof for delivering the contract copy and cannot later invoke contract invalidity to the consumer's detriment.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
key_items: Cayma Hakkının Kullanımı ve Tarafların Yükümlülükleri
nodes.summary: The text covers Chapter 3 (Right of Withdrawal and Parties' Obligations) and Chapter 4 (Special Provisions for Long-Term Holiday Service Contracts) of a Turkish regulation on timeshare and long-term holiday service contracts. Key points: consumers have a 14-day withdrawal right without reason or penalty; withdrawal must be notified in writing or via permanent data storage (or via notary for real estate); sellers must provide a withdrawal form and cannot demand payment before the withdrawal period expires; all related contracts (resale, exchange) terminate automatically upon withdrawal; refunds must be made within 14 days. If the seller fails to meet information obligations, the 14-day period is extended up to one year. Linked credit contracts also terminate without penalty if the consumer withdraws and notifies the lender. For long-term holiday service contracts (over one year), payments must be structured as equal annual installments, sellers must notify consumers at least 14 days before each payment, and consumers may terminate without penalty from the third year onward within 14 days of receiving a payment notification.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM
key_items: ALTINCI BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 5 (Prepaid Timeshare Contracts) and Chapter 6 (Miscellaneous and Final Provisions) of a Turkish regulation. Article 14 outlines general principles: mandatory document delivery (floor plans, site plans), guarantee requirements for projects exceeding 1 million TL, consumer's unconditional right to withdraw before transfer, withdrawal notification methods (written/notary), max 2% compensation, 90-day refund and 10-day return deadlines, credit-related refund procedures, project change notification with withdrawal rights, building permit prerequisite, and seller's burden of proof. Article 15 addresses prepaid sale of real rights (ayni hak), requiring registration of co-ownership or notary sale promise, with a 36-month transfer limit and usability conditions. Article 16 covers prepaid sale of personal rights (şahsi hak), also with a 36-month deadline and usability requirement. Chapter 6 declares exemption clauses invalid (Art. 17), repeals the 2003 regulation (Art. 18), sets the effective date as publication date (Art. 19), and assigns execution to the Minister of Customs and Trade (Art. 20).

summary: This section presents a sample cancellation form for off-premises contracts and the full text of three Turkish consumer protection regulations published in the Official Gazette. First, the Distance Contracts Regulation (2014) covers purpose, scope (excluding financial services, real estate, gambling, etc.), legal basis (Law No. 6502), definitions, pre-contractual information obligations (content, 12-point font, delivery methods, confirmation), the 14-day withdrawal right with refund/return duties, exceptions, and final provisions. Second, the Financial Services Distance Contracts Regulation (2015) addresses purpose, scope, definitions, pre-information requirements (risks, fees, withdrawal conditions), withdrawal procedures, and final provisions. Third, the Timeshare and Long-term Holiday Service Contracts Regulation covers purpose, scope, definitions, pre-contractual information forms, contract requirements, the 14-day withdrawal right, linked credit contract termination, long-term holiday installment rules, prepaid timeshare guarantees and transfer deadlines, invalidity of exemption clauses, and final provisions. Each regulation includes a sample cancellation form appendix.

title: EK - 1
summary: This text is Appendix 1 of the Turkish Regulation on Timeshare and Long-Term Holiday Service Contracts, presenting a mandatory pre-information form for timeshare contracts. It lists required disclosure items (a–r) including: seller/provider identification; definition and scope of the right; contract duration and usage period; property condition and location; total price with taxes; common facility costs and their calculation/increase mechanisms; available amenities (pool, sauna, etc.); maintenance and management arrangements with consumer participation; assurance of no hidden obligations; transfer/exchange possibilities; 14-day withdrawal right with contact details; legal restrictions on the property; specific withdrawal statements for timeshare and other real/personal rights contracts; withdrawal rights if consumer is not properly informed; termination conditions and consequences; third-party benefit provisions; complaint resolution methods; consumer court/arbitration information; payment plan and bank details; and installment sale terms including total price, interest rates, default consequences, and down payment.

title: EK - 2
summary: This text is Appendix 2 of Turkey's Regulation on Holiday Exchange and Long-Term Holiday Service Contracts, presenting a mandatory pre-information form for long-term holiday service agreements. It requires disclosure of: seller/provider identification details (name, address, MERSIS number); service nature, scope, duration, and usage conditions; service start date; any additional expenses; an installment payment plan with equal annual amounts and payment deadlines; post-first-year installment increase rates; main service details; withdrawal right procedures and contact information; a mandatory 14-day no-penalty withdrawal statement; extended withdrawal rights if the consumer was inadequately informed (up to one year after the withdrawal period); the right to terminate without penalty within 14 days after the second installment payment notice; assurance of no hidden additional payments or obligations; complaint resolution methods; the consumer's right to file disputes with consumer courts or arbitration boards; and information on priorities, promotions, special discounts, and potential restrictions.

title: EK - 3
key_items: YENİDEN SATIŞ SÖZLEŞMELERİNE İLİŞKİN ÖN BİLGİLENDİRME FORMU
summary: This text is Appendix 3 of a regulation, specifying the mandatory contents of a Pre-Information Form for Resale Contracts. It lists required items (a–i): seller/provider identification and contact details; nature, scope, and usage conditions of the service; contract duration; total price including all taxes; any additional costs; withdrawal right procedures and contact information; a mandatory 14-day no-reason withdrawal statement with a commitment not to demand payment during that period; information that the 14-day period extends to one year if the consumer was not properly informed; assurance that the service entails no extra payments or obligations; whether contract rights can be resold via a system and related costs; complaint resolution methods; and the consumer's right to file disputes with consumer courts or arbitration boards.

title: EK - 4 DEĞİŞİM SÖZLEŞMELERİNE İLİŞKİN ÖN BİLGİLENDİRME FORMU
summary: This text is Appendix 4 of the Turkish Regulation on Timeshare and Long-Term Holiday Service Contracts, presenting a mandatory pre-information form for exchange contracts. It lists required disclosures (items a–n) including: seller/provider identification details; nature, scope, and usage conditions of the contractual right; contract duration and usage period; total price including taxes; additional consumer costs; explanation of the exchange system's operation and options; differences between exchange rights; main services' nature and scope; right of withdrawal procedures and contact details; the mandatory 14-day withdrawal statement with a no-payment guarantee; extended withdrawal period if consumer is not properly informed; single withdrawal period when bundled with a timeshare contract; benefits and restrictions for the consumer; non-real-estate accommodation information; complaint resolution methods; consumer court/arbitration options; and termination conditions with their consequences.

title: EK - 5
key_items: ÖN ÖDEMELİ DEVRE TATİL SÖZLEŞMELERİNE İLİŞKİN ÖN BİLGİLENDİRME FORMU
summary: This text is Appendix 5 of the Timeshare and Long-Term Holiday Service Contracts Regulation, listing mandatory items for the Pre-Information Form of pre-paid timeshare contracts. It requires disclosure of: seller/provider/owner contact details; definition and scope of the right; contract duration and usage period; property condition and location; total price including taxes; common facility costs and their calculation/increase mechanisms; available amenities and services; maintenance and management arrangements with consumer participation; assurance of no hidden obligations; transfer/exchange possibilities; 14-day withdrawal rights (with specific wording for timeshare vs. other rights contracts); pre-payment amount; guarantee details; building permit date; 36-month delivery limit; rescission rights with max 2% penalty; termination conditions and consequences; complaint resolution methods; consumer court/arbitration options; payment plan and bank details; and installment sale terms including total price, interest rates, default consequences, and down payment.

nodes.title: EK - 6 ÖRNEK CAYMA FORMU (intro)
nodes.summary: This text presents Appendix 6 (EK-6) of the Package Tour Contracts Regulation (Paket Tur Sözleşmeleri Yönetmeliği), which is a sample cancellation form. The form is to be completed and submitted only when a consumer wishes to exercise their right to cancel a contract. It includes a 'To' section for the seller/provider's name, title, address, fax, and email. The form contains a declaration of exercising the cancellation right, followed by fields for: contract date, the right or service subject to cancellation, its price, the consumer's full name, address, signature (required only for paper submissions), and date. The document is published in the Official Gazette (Resmî Gazete), Issue 29236, dated January 14, 2015 (Wednesday), on page 168.

nodes.title: PAKET TUR SÖZLEŞMELERİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Package Tour Contracts Regulation, covering: (1) Purpose – establishing procedures and principles for package tour contracts; (2) Scope – applying to all package tour/holiday/travel contracts, including those with separately billed services, those organized abroad but sold in Turkey via agents, and those involving commercial/professional users; (3) Legal basis – Articles 51 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502, 2013); (4) Definitions – defining key terms: independent service provider, other tourism services (vehicle rental, cultural tours, shows, sports, guiding), permanent data storage, participant, package tour agent, package tour organizer, package tour contract (requiring at least two of transport, accommodation, and other tourism services sold at an all-inclusive price, lasting over 24 hours or including overnight stay), and consumer.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
MADDE 5
nodes.summary: This text is Article 5 of the Second Chapter on Contract and Information Obligations, detailing the brochure provision requirement for package tours. It mandates that a brochure must be provided to participants before contract formation. The brochure must include the total price (taxes included), prepayment amount, remaining payment date, and, where applicable: journey start/end dates and locations; transport type, class, and schedule; accommodation details (type, location, class, and classification warnings); meal plan; route; passport, visa, age, and health requirements; minimum participant number and cancellation deadline; mandatory and additional insurance information; and tour guide services. The brochure content is binding on the organizer and intermediary. Changes to brochure information are permitted before contract formation (if clearly stated and notified) or after contract formation (with mutual agreement of both parties).

nodes.title: Package Tour Contract Obligations and Pre-Trip Information
nodes.summary: The text covers Articles 6 and 7 of the Package Tour Contracts Regulation. Article 6 mandates that organizers or agents must draft a written package tour contract with participants, specifying required content: parties' identities and contact details, destinations with dates, total price in Turkish Lira (or foreign currency for international tours), price change conditions, payment plan, accepted special requests, force majeure provisions, and cancellation/termination terms. Article 7 requires pre-trip information to be provided at least 24 hours before domestic tours and 48 hours before foreign tours, covering: departure/arrival details, intermediate stops, assigned locations, local representative or contact point information, communication details for minors traveling abroad, and optional insurance details. Re-information is not required if the brochure or contract already contains unchanged information.

nodes.title: Sözleşme ve bilgilendirmenin şekli
nodes.summary:
Yönetmelikler
Sözleşme ve bilgilendirmenin şekli
MADDE 8 – (1) Yazılı veya mesafeli olarak kurulan paket tur sözleşmeleri ile bu Yönetmelik kapsamında yapılan bilgilendirmelerin, en az on iki punto büyüklüğünde, anlaşılabilir bir dilde, açık, sade ve okunabilir bir şekilde düzenlenmesi ve bunların bir örneğinin kâğıt üzerinde veya kalıcı veri saklayıcısı ile katılımcıya verilmesi zorunludur.

This section (Second Chapter) covers contract and information obligations for package tours. Article 5 mandates providing a detailed brochure before contract formation, specifying price, dates, transport, accommodation, meals, route, participant requirements, insurance, and tour guide services, with rules for modifying brochure content. Articles 6 and 7 require a written contract detailing parties' identities, destinations, pricing, payment plans, force majeure, and cancellation terms, along with pre-trip information provided at least 24 hours before domestic and 48 hours before foreign tours, covering departure details, local contacts, and communication for minors. Article 8 stipulates that all contracts and information must be in at least 12-point font, written in clear, understandable language, and provided to participants on paper or via permanent data storage.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 3 of the Package Tour Contracts Regulation, covering three main topics: (1) Price changes (Article 9): Prices may be altered up to 5% of the contract value only if explicitly stated in the contract, with written notice at least 20 days before departure, due to extraordinary currency fluctuations (for foreign tours), fuel cost changes, or changes in taxes/fees at ports/airports. (2) Essential contract changes (Article 10): Significant changes not caused by the participant (excluding Article 9 price changes) are deemed essential. The organizer must notify the participant immediately. The participant may accept the change, join an equivalent or higher-value tour at no extra cost, join a lower-value tour with a price-difference refund, or cancel without compensation. Upon cancellation, the organizer must refund the full amount within 14 days. (3) Package tour cancellation (Article 11): If the organizer cancels for reasons not attributable to the participant, the participant may exercise the rights granted under Article 10(3).

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 4 of a package tour regulation, addressing non-performance of contract obligations. Article 12 (Incomplete Performance) requires participants to immediately report deficiencies; if unresolved, they may request price reduction. If the organizer fails key obligations post-tour-start, they must offer equivalent alternatives at no extra cost and compensate differences. Participants may terminate the contract, triggering refund within 14 days (less fair compensation for services already rendered), plus free transport back and mandatory accommodation costs. Article 13 (Liability) holds the organizer/agent liable for all damages from non-performance, including wasted vacation time, even when breach stems from independent service providers. Article 14 (Exemption from Liability) exempts the organizer when breach results from: participant's fault, unforeseeable third-party acts, force majeure, unforeseeable events despite due care, or cancellation due to unmet minimum participation (notified 20+ days prior). In the latter three cases, the organizer must still provide prompt assistance to participants in difficulty.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM
Katılımcının Diğer Hakları
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 5 on additional participant rights in a package tour contract, addressing two main topics. Article 15 (Transfer of Contract): A participant may transfer the contract to a qualifying third party at least seven days before the tour begins, with written or permanent data storage notice. Both parties are jointly liable for the remaining balance and reasonable additional transfer costs, which cannot exceed the organizer's actual costs. Article 16 (Termination of Contract): A participant may unilaterally terminate with written notice. If terminated 30+ days before departure, a full refund is due except mandatory taxes and fees. If terminated less than 30 days before, contractual deductions may apply. In cases of unforeseeable, unavoidable circumstances or force majeure within 30 days, a full refund is owed except for mandatory taxes, fees, and documented non-refundable third-party payments. All refunds must be processed within 14 days of the termination notice reaching the organizer or agent.

nodes.title: ALTINCI BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers the final provisions (Chapter 6) of Turkey's Package Tour Contracts Regulation. It addresses: (1) Agent liability when the organizer lacks a Turkish representative (Art. 17); (2) Invalidity of any clause waiving participant rights or limiting organizer/agent obligations (Art. 18); (3) Repeal of the 2003 prior regulation (Art. 19); (4) Entry into force upon publication (Art. 20); (5) Execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade (Art. 21); (6) A temporary provision on COVID-19-related cancellations, specifying refund timelines—14 days normally, or 14 days after the 60th day post-flight-ban-lifting for air-inclusive tours from 5/2/2020—with participant consent requirements and burden of proof on the organizer/agent; and (7) Publication details (Official Gazette No. 29236, 14/1/2015) and amendment reference (No. 31128, 15/5/2020).

nodes.title: ABONELİK SÖZLEŞMELERİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Subscription Contracts Regulation, covering: (1) Purpose – establishing procedures and principles for subscription contracts; (2) Scope – applying to all subscription contracts where consumers acquire goods or services continuously or at regular intervals, with limited application (only Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 13, 22, 23, 24, 25) to sectors other than electricity, water, natural gas, and electronic communication; (3) Legal basis – grounded in Articles 52 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 (2013); and (4) Definitions – defining key terms including subscription contract, Minister, electronic communication, late payment interest rate, service, permanent data storage, Law, goods, provider, seller, and consumer.

This section covers three regulatory areas. First, additional participant rights in package tour contracts, including contract transfer to a third party (Art. 15) with joint liability for remaining balance and transfer costs, and unilateral termination (Art. 16) with refund conditions based on timing (30+ days vs. less than 30 days before departure), force majeure provisions, and a 14-day refund processing deadline. Second, final provisions of Turkey's Package Tour Contracts Regulation (Chapter 6), addressing agent liability, invalidity of rights-waiving clauses, repeal of the 2003 regulation, entry into force, execution authority, a temporary COVID-19 cancellation provision with specific refund timelines, and publication/amendment references. Third, the first chapter of Turkey's Subscription Contracts Regulation, defining its purpose, scope (continuous or periodic goods/services acquisition), legal basis under Consumer Protection Law No. 6502, and key definitions including subscription contract, provider, consumer, and related terms.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 2 on the form and content of subscription contracts. Article 5 requires sellers to establish a written or distance subscription contract, provided to consumers on paper or permanent data storage, in at least 12-point font, clear and readable language. Article 6 lists mandatory contract content (items a–n), including parties' identification, subject, duration, date, delivery/start date, total price, tariff details, service suspension/resumption procedures, meter/modem change rights, force majeure causes, consumer rights for defective goods/services, meter malfunction handling, mandatory fees, default consequences, deposit/guarantee terms, termination conditions, device return procedures, and dispute resolution options. Exceptions apply: non-utility/telecom contracts may omit certain items, and electricity/water/gas contracts need not include delivery date info. Article 7 states that missing mandatory elements do not invalidate the contract; the seller must rectify deficiencies immediately without extra charges, otherwise the consumer may terminate without penalty or compensation.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of the Subscription Contracts Regulation, detailing the seller/provider's obligations. It addresses: (1) Delivery/Performance (Art. 8): the provider must deliver goods/services per contract; billing begins only upon actual service provision, except for prepaid services. (2) Notification (Art. 9): at least 48 hours' prior written or media notice is required for planned maintenance, repairs, or service interruptions. (3) Information (Art. 10): providers must supply contract copies, commitment documents, and tariff details free of charge upon request or via their website. (4) Billing Period (Art. 11): default period is one month; billing may be deferred if consumption falls below agreed amounts; unit prices cannot be increased by altering the billing period. (5) Late Payment (Art. 12): late-payment penalties cannot exceed the rate set under Article 51 of Law No. 6183. (6) Other Obligations (Art. 13): automatic renewal clauses are prohibited; renewal requires consumer consent; no charges apply if service continues without explicit consumer request; electronic communication providers share responsibility with value-added service providers.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter Four on Committed Subscription Principles (Articles 14-18). Article 14 defines committed subscriptions as arrangements where sellers/providers offer discounts or transfer ownership/usage rights in exchange for a fixed subscription period, prohibiting unfavorable changes during the commitment. Article 15 mandates a written commitment document containing validity period, product/service details, total price with taxes, pre-commitment pricing, monthly discounts, and early-termination cost calculation methods; it specifies delivery rules for voice or limited-time/space commitments (14-day deadline) and caps prices at non-committed levels. Article 16 limits early-termination charges to uncollected discounts, devices, or benefits, using whichever is lower for the consumer, and allows free termination if relocation makes service delivery impossible. Article 17 requires written notification at least one billing period before termination. Article 18 holds service providers liable for defects in goods transferred alongside services.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: Chapter 5 outlines payment notification rules. Article 19 requires sellers/providers to issue a payment notification at the end of each consumption period, containing minimum information: consumer identity, period, meter readings, consumption amount, unit price, tariff details, total amount with taxes, past debts/credits, payment deadline, payment methods, complaint channels, late penalty rate, and commitment period details. Invoices may serve as notifications. Information must be clear and readable, and sellers must offer online display or free electronic delivery. Article 20 mandates sending the notification at least seven days before the payment deadline, optionally via persistent data storage, with no cost to the consumer. Article 21 allows consumers to object to incorrect amounts within one year; sellers must resolve within 30 days. Valid objections result in refund within five days or deduction from the next bill, including late payment penalties.

nodes.title: ALTINCI BÖLÜM
key_items: YEDİNCİ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 6 (Termination of Subscription Contracts and Consequences) and Chapter 7 (Miscellaneous and Final Provisions) of a Turkish Subscription Contracts Regulation. It details: consumer rights to terminate indefinite or long-term (≥1 year) contracts without penalty; termination conditions for short-term contracts; seller obligations to maintain termination processing systems; acceptable termination notice methods (written, permanent data storage, phone) without imposing heavier conditions than contract formation; fulfillment deadlines (7 days generally; 15 days/1 month/3 months for daily/weekly/monthly publications); consequences including written confirmation, no charges for unfulfilled periods, refund within 15 days, payment notification within 10 days (up to 4 months for telecom), and offsetting without extra cost. Chapter 7 addresses phone line fee limitations, entry into force (3 months post-publication), and execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade. Published in the Official Gazette on June 18, 2014 (No. 29034).

nodes.title: SÜRELİ YAYIN KURULUŞLARINCA DÜZENLENEN PROMOSYON UYGULAMALARINA İLİŞKİN YÖNETMELİK BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM
Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of a Turkish regulation governing promotional activities organized by periodical publications. It covers four key points: (1) Purpose – to establish the procedures and principles for such promotional activities; (2) Scope – covering promotions organized by periodical publications or those directly/indirectly associated with them, even if not organized by them; (3) Legal basis – grounded in Articles 53 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 (dated 7/11/2013); and (4) Definitions – defining 'promotional activity' as providing goods or services linked directly or indirectly to periodical publications, and 'periodical publication' as newspapers, magazines, or similar works published at regular intervals in print or downloadable electronically.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM Genel Esaslar
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 2 (General Principles) of a Turkish regulation governing promotion practices by periodical publications. Article 5 defines permissible promotional items (books, maps, flags, calendars, puzzles, chess sets, event tickets, cultural tours, language education, optical discs) and excludes single-use items not requiring multiple purchases. Article 6 sets promotion duration limits (75 days for daily, 18 weeks for weekly, 12 months for longer periodicals), with exceptions for subscriptions, and mandates 10% backup coupons for coupon-based promotions. Article 7 requires publishers to publicly announce delivery dates and locations. Article 8 mandates delivery within 45 days after the promotion ends and prohibits charging consumers additional fees. Article 9 prohibits price increases due to promotion costs, bans splitting promotional items, treats each item as an independent promotion, and defines national distribution as covering at least 70% of the population, with electronic publications automatically considered national.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text is the final chapter (Chapter 3) of the Price Label Regulation (Fiyat Etiketi Yönetmeliği), published in the Official Gazette on June 28, 2014 (Issue 29044). It covers three points: (1) A transitional provision (Temporary Article 1) stating that promotional practices initiated before the regulation's effective date are exempt from its provisions. (2) Article 10 specifying that the regulation enters into force on the date of its publication. (3) Article 11 designating the Minister of Customs and Trade as the authority responsible for executing the regulation's provisions.

nodes.title: FİYAT ETİKETİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Price Label Regulation, covering its purpose, scope, legal basis, and definitions. The purpose is to regulate the form, content, and use of labels, tariffs, and price lists for retail goods and services, as well as discounted sale procedures. The scope encompasses all consumer-facing labels, tariffs, and price lists. The legal basis is Articles 54 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502). The definitions section defines key terms including: open-sold goods, the Ministry (Customs and Trade), label (price label with taxes, unit price, production place, and distinguishing features), service, discounted sale, goods (movable property, real estate, software, intangible goods), unit price, production place, sale price, provider, seller, tariff/price list, consumer, domestic production (goods produced in Turkey under specific laws), and the domestic production logo (Ministry-designated mark for Turkish-made goods).

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM Genel Esaslar
nodes.summary: This text covers Articles 5-10 of Turkey's Price Label Regulation (Fiyat Etiketi Yönetmeliği), Chapter 2 (General Principles). It mandates visible, readable labels (written, digital, or electronic) on retail goods, specifying required information: production place, distinguishing feature, total tax-inclusive price, unit price, effective date, and local production logo. Imported goods must display the country in Turkish. Specific packaging types require both sale and unit prices; open goods need only unit price. Service tariffs follow similar rules. Article 6 exempts goods with pre-printed info, publications, auction items, and exchange-priced precious stones (which still require visible unit prices and labor cost disclosure). Article 7 addresses label placement methods. Article 8 requires visible tariff/price lists including any additional fees. Article 9 stipulates labels must be readable, accurate, non-misleading, and clearly identifiable; prices must be in Turkish Lira (with exceptions for certain international services). Article 10 states the consumer-favorable price applies when sale and register prices differ, and different units must display separate prices.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 3 (Various and Final Provisions) of Turkey's Price Label Regulation. It covers: (1) Discounted sales rules requiring display of both discounted and pre-discount prices on labels, tariffs, and price lists, with the seller bearing the burden of proof for prior pricing, and time limits of 3 months (business changes) or 6 months (liquidation) for such sales; (2) Combined wholesale-retail sales, where retail regulations apply; (3) Supervision duties assigned to the Ministry, municipalities, and relevant chambers, with violations referred to the provincial governor; (4) Repeal of the 2003 Label, Tariff and Price List Regulation; (5) Entry into force upon publication; (6) Execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade. It also lists the Official Gazette publication date (28/6/2014, No. 29044), two amendment dates (2018 and 2019), and references the Introduction and User Manual Regulation (13/6/2014, No. 29029).

nodes.title: TANITMA VE KULLANMA KILAVUZU YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of a Turkish regulation on Introduction and Use Guides. It covers: (1) Purpose – establishing procedures for guides covering introduction, use, installation, maintenance, and simple repair of consumer goods; (2) Scope – applies to all consumer goods except those in Article 6; (3) Legal basis – Articles 55 and 84 of Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 (2013); (4) Definitions – defining key terms including Ministry (of Trade), Importer, Permanent Data Storage (SMS, email, disk, CD, DVD, memory card, etc.), Law, User Interface, Goods (movable items requiring Turkish guides), Seller, Introduction and Use Guide (including labels with international symbols), Consumer (non-commercial actors), and Producer (manufacturers or entities placing their mark on goods).

nodes.title: Tanıtma ve Kullanma Kılavuzu Düzenleme ve Uygulama Esasları
nodes.summary: This text covers the Turkish Regulation on Introduction and User Manuals (Articles 5-11). Article 5 mandates that goods sold to consumers must include a Turkish-language manual in clear, readable form (paper or permanent data storage), with access information on packaging and the manufacturer's website; user interface text/audio/visuals must be in Turkish. Article 6 lists exempt goods (pipes, fasteners, stationery, agricultural/mechanical tools, clothing accessories, construction materials, kitchen/household items, handicrafts, measuring instruments, replacement parts, and packaged goods with specs on packaging). Article 7 specifies required manual content: manufacturer/importer contact details, usage/installation/maintenance rules, transport precautions, error info, product features, periodic maintenance, montage diagrams, service life, authorized service station info, consumer rights, complaint procedures, and energy efficiency info for energy-consuming goods; safety warnings must be in Turkish. Article 8 assigns preparation responsibility to manufacturers/importers and delivery proof to sellers. Articles 9-11 repeal the 2003 regulation, set entry-into-force dates, and designate the Minister of Trade as executor.

nodes.title: GARANTİ BELGESİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Kapsam, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Warranty Certificate Regulation (Garanti Belgesi Yönetmeliği), covering Purpose, Scope, Legal Basis, and Definitions. The purpose is to identify goods requiring warranty certificates and regulate related procedures. The scope covers goods listed in the annex. The legal basis is Articles 56 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502). The definitions section defines key terms: maximum repair period, Ministry (Ministry of Trade), warranty certificate, General Directorate (Consumer Protection and Market Surveillance), working day, importer, the Law, goods, seller, manufacturer, authorized service station, and permanent data storage device. Each definition specifies the role or meaning of the term within the regulation's context, including amendments made in 2020.

This section covers four Turkish consumer protection regulations grounded in the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502: (1) Promotional Activities by Periodical Publications – defining purpose, scope, permissible promotional items, duration limits, delivery obligations, and prohibitions on price increases; (2) Price Label Regulation – governing the form, content, and display of labels, tariffs, and price lists for retail goods and services, including discounted sale rules, exemptions, and supervision duties; (3) Introduction and Use Guide Regulation – mandating Turkish-language manuals for consumer goods, specifying required content (usage, maintenance, safety, energy efficiency), listing exempt items, and assigning preparation responsibilities; and (4) Warranty Certificate Regulation – identifying goods requiring warranty certificates and defining related terms and procedures. Each regulation includes its legal basis, definitions, general principles, and final provisions regarding entry into force and execution authority.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers the Second Chapter on principles for issuing warranty certificates. Article 5 mandates that manufacturers and importers must issue clear, readable warranty certificates for unused goods listed in the regulation's annex. The seller is responsible for completing and delivering the certificate, which can be provided on paper or via permanent data storage; paper is mandatory upon consumer request. Invoices cannot substitute warranty certificates. Article 6 defines the warranty period as starting from delivery, lasting a minimum of two years or the value specified by the annex's measurement unit. If an alternative unit is used, the product must have a mechanism to measure it; otherwise, the minimum is two years. Repair time is added to the warranty period. Article 7 lists mandatory information in the certificate: manufacturer/importer and seller details with signatures, invoice number, product identification, delivery date/place, warranty period, maximum repair time, full coverage statement, consumer's optional rights, usage error information, complaint procedures, and other consumer rights. Exceptions apply for distance contracts and electronic delivery.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 (Consumer's Warranty Rights) and Chapter 4 (Final Provisions) of a Turkish Warranty Certificate Regulation. Chapter 3 addresses: (1) the right to free repair, where the seller must repair the product without any charge, and the consumer may also claim this against the manufacturer or importer, all being jointly liable; (2) additional consumer rights including refund, proportional price reduction, or replacement if the product malfunctions again, exceeds maximum repair time, or is deemed unrepairable by an official report, with the seller unable to refuse and replacement required within 30 working days; (3) the warranty period of a replaced product being limited to the remaining warranty of the original; and (4) usage errors, where warranty rights do not apply if malfunction results from consumer misuse, with the error to be confirmed by an official report and subject to expert review. Chapter 4 states the 2003 regulation is repealed, the new regulation takes effect upon publication, and is executed by the Minister of Commerce.

summary: This section covers multiple Turkish consumer protection regulations. It begins with a sample cancellation form (EK-6) for package tour contracts. It then details the Package Tour Contracts Regulation: purpose, scope, definitions, contract/information obligations, price changes, essential changes, cancellation rights, non-performance liability, participant rights (transfer, termination), and final provisions. The section continues with the Subscription Contracts Regulation: contract form/content, provider obligations (delivery, notification, billing, late payment), committed subscription principles, payment notification rules, termination procedures, and final provisions. Finally, it addresses four additional regulations: promotional activities by periodical publications, price label requirements, introduction/use guide mandates, and warranty certificate regulations (issuing principles, consumer warranty rights including free repair, replacement, refund, and final provisions). All are grounded in Consumer Protection Law No. 6502.

title: EK -1

nodes.title: EK -1 (intro)
nodes.summary: This text is Appendix 1 (EK-1) of the Guarantee Certificate Regulation, listing products that must be sold with a guarantee certificate under Turkey's Consumer Protection Law No. 6502. All listed products carry a 2-year guarantee period. The categories include: (1) Health Products, subdivided into personal use devices (blood pressure monitors, blood value measuring devices, hearing aids, speech devices, thermometers, massage tools), mother and child products (electronic breast pumps, bottle warmers, sterilizers, baby food preparation sets, child car seats, high chairs, strollers, baby monitoring cameras), and devices for disabled persons (wheelchairs, electric vehicles, book readers for visually impaired); (2) Glasses (sunglasses and eyeglass frames); and (3) Heating and Ventilation Devices (air conditioners, heat pumps, fan coils, burners, heating boilers, floor heaters, combi boilers, natural gas/LPG stoves, kerosene stoves, solid fuel stoves, electric room heaters, and water heaters).
