nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's After-Sales Services Regulation, covering: (1) Purpose – regulating usage lifetimes, maximum repair durations, and after-sales assembly, maintenance, and repair procedures for listed goods; (2) Scope – applying to manufacturers/importers obligated to provide after-sales services and independent service stations; (3) Legal basis – Articles 58 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502, 2013); and (4) Definitions – defining key terms including maximum repair time, Ministry of Trade, General Directorate, Provincial Directorate, working day, importer, usage lifetime, goods, private service, seller, after-sales service qualification certificate, service station, consumer, manufacturer, authorized service station, and permanent data storage device.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
MADDE 5
nodes.summary: This text is from the Second Chapter on Principles Related to Service Stations and Service Services. Article 5, paragraph 1, mandates that manufacturers or importers must establish authorized service stations with adequate technical staff for each product group specified in the attached list, covering the designated usage life period, at the locations, quantities, and specifications outlined in that list, in order to provide after-sales services. Paragraph 2 states that manufacturers or importers may either set up their own service stations or utilize existing service stations or service organizations, provided they remain responsible for the services rendered.

nodes.title: Başvuru ve izin
nodes.summary: The text covers Articles 6-9 of a Turkish regulation on after-sales service competency certification. Article 6 mandates that manufacturers/importers obtain a competency certificate for listed goods (except those not requiring service stations), with applications submitted electronically via the Ministry website. The General Directorate reviews applications for legal compliance and may request reports from approved bodies. Article 7 sets a two-year validity period requiring renewal, specifies documentation for changes (name, address, service station, scope), and requires reporting service changes within 30 days. Article 8 provides for certificate cancellation if non-compliance persists after a written warning and correction deadline. Article 9 establishes that authorized service stations must meet Ministry or Turkish Standards Institute requirements; their number and features are determined by the General Directorate based on product characteristics, usage, and sales volume. Control inspections are conducted by designated personnel or authorized institutions, and compliance certificates are issued to sufficient stations. Additional stations beyond the required number must also comply with the regulation.

nodes.title: Servis istasyonlarının sorumlulukları
nodes.summary: This text covers Articles 10-14 of Turkey's After-Sales Services Regulation. Article 10 defines service station responsibilities: the nearest authorized station serves consumers if none exists locally; no transport/cargo fees during warranty; mandatory document issuance; maximum repair time limits with notification methods and proof-of-burden rules; no charges for recurring faults within one year outside warranty; minimum six-month warranty on replaced parts. Article 11 specifies required documents: a receipt document (names, signatures, complaints, product details, delivery date) and a service invoice (station info, repair details, fees, consumer details), with provisions for electronic delivery via permanent data storage and exemptions for on-site repairs. Article 12 mandates spare parts availability and visible price lists. Article 13 requires showing or returning replaced parts to consumers. Article 14 establishes joint and several liability of manufacturers/importers with service stations and allows on-site service provision.

nodes.title: Service Station Documents, Spare Parts, and Replaced Parts Regulations
nodes.summary: The page covers requirements for service station documents (servis fişi), including mandatory information such as station details, delivery date, fault description, fees, signatures, and consumer data. It notes exceptions for special service providers, on-site repairs, and the option to use reports instead of separate documents. It also addresses electronic delivery of documents via persistent data storage, signature requirements, and the burden of proof on service stations. MADDE 12 states that manufacturers/importers must sell spare parts upon consumer request, and service stations must display spare parts price lists visibly or electronically. MADDE 13 requires authorized service stations to show replaced parts to consumers within the warranty period or return them outside the warranty period, subject to environmental law provisions.

nodes.title: Üretici, ithalatçı ve satıcının sorumluluğu
nodes.summary: Article 14 of the After-Sales Services Regulation outlines the responsibilities of manufacturers, importers, and sellers. Key points include: (1) joint liability of manufacturers/importers with authorized service stations for after-sales services; (2) services may be provided at the product's place of use; (3) no transport or service fees may be charged during warranty (except for misuse per manual); (4) if repair exceeds 10 business days, a similar replacement product must be provided, with proof burden on the manufacturer/importer; (5) if an importer ceases operations, seller, manufacturer, and new importer share joint liability during warranty, and manufacturer/new importer must maintain the product for its lifespan; (6) manufacturers/importers must monitor and control service stations; (7) sellers must issue a receipt for defective goods; (8) website operators must list all service station contacts; (9) all service station data must be entered into the Ministry's Service Information System within 30 days and kept updated.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 3 (Various and Final Provisions) of a Turkish regulation on after-sales services. It covers: (1) Exemption (Art. 15): the regulation does not apply to non-commercial personal-use production/import or goods made per consumer special orders; (2) Document retention (Art. 16): all information/documents related to regulated operations must be kept for three years; (3) Repeal (Art. 17): the 2003 regulation on after-sales services for industrial goods is repealed; (4) Transitional provisions (Temp. Art. 1): previously approved after-sales service qualification certificates remain valid for two years from approval, and for new products lacking standards, a certificate must be obtained within three months of the relevant standard entering into force; (5) Entry into force (Art. 18): the regulation takes effect on its publication date; (6) Execution (Art. 19): the Minister of Commerce is responsible for implementing the regulation's provisions.

This section (Second Chapter) of Turkey's After-Sales Services Regulation covers: (1) Mandatory establishment of authorized service stations by manufacturers/importers with adequate technical staff (Art. 5); (2) Competency certification requirements, application procedures, two-year validity, renewal, cancellation for non-compliance, and service station standards with control inspections (Arts. 6-9); (3) Service station responsibilities including consumer service obligations, repair time limits, warranty on replaced parts, required documentation (receipts, service invoices), spare parts availability with visible price lists, and showing/returning replaced parts (Arts. 10-13); (4) Joint and several liability of manufacturers/importers with service stations, on-site service options, replacement product requirements for delayed repairs, liability allocation when importers cease operations, seller and website operator obligations, and mandatory data entry into the Ministry's Service Information System (Art. 14); (5) Chapter 3 provisions on exemptions, three-year document retention, repeal of the 2003 regulation, transitional provisions for existing certificates, entry into force, and execution by the Minister of Commerce (Arts. 15-19, Temp. Art. 1).

summary: This section (EK-1) comprises Appendix 1 of Turkey's Guarantee Certificate Regulation and the After-Sales Services Regulation. The appendix lists products requiring a 2-year guarantee under Consumer Protection Law No. 6502, including health products (personal devices, mother/child items, disabled-person aids), glasses, heating/ventilation devices, water heaters, fans, air purifiers, sanitary plumbing products (pumps, valves, bathtubs, jacuzzis, toilets, sinks), and portable electric hand tools. The After-Sales Services Regulation's first chapter defines its purpose (regulating usage lifetimes, repair durations, after-sales procedures), scope, legal basis, and key terms. The second chapter mandates authorized service stations with certified staff, sets service station responsibilities (repair limits, part warranties, documentation, spare parts availability), establishes joint manufacturer/importer liability, and includes final provisions on exemptions, document retention, transitional measures, and entry into force.

title: EK

nodes.title: EK (intro)
nodes.summary: This text is an appendix to Turkey's After-Sales Services Regulation (under Consumer Protection Law No. 6502), listing products requiring mandatory after-sales service. It specifies for each product: usage life, maximum repair time (uniformly 20 working days), and service point requirements (number and geographic distribution). Covered categories include: (1) Health products—personal devices (blood pressure monitors, hearing aids, thermometers, massage devices), mother/child items (breast pumps, bottle warmers, car seats, strollers, baby monitors), and disabled persons' devices (wheelchairs, electric vehicles, book readers); (2) Eyeglasses and frames; (3) Heating/ventilation equipment (ACs, boilers, heaters, fans, hoods, humidifiers); (4) Plumbing products (pumps, valves, faucets, bathtubs, jacuzzis, toilets, sinks); (5) Portable electric hand tools (saws, drills, polishers); (6) Motors (electric, combustion, marine); and (7) Alternative energy systems (solar, wind). Service requirements range from 1 service point to 30 services across 7 geographic regions, with some items requiring no service.

nodes.title: Warranty Periods for Plumbing, Hand Tools, and Motors
key_items: 4.8 KÜVET VE DUŞ TEKNELERİ HİDROMASAJ SİSTEMLERİ VE 4.9 JAKUZİLER
nodes.summary: The text lists mandatory warranty periods under the After-Sales Services Regulation for three product categories. Plumbing fixtures (batteries, taps, reservoirs, bathtubs, hydromassage systems, jacuzzis, shower cabins, electric saunas, lavatories, toilets, sinks) carry 5- or 10-year warranties. Portable electric hand tools (saw machines, polishing machines, drills, soldering guns, screwdriving machines, sanding machines, palm grinding machines) all carry 7-year warranties. Motors (electric motors and internal combustion engines) carry 10-year warranties.

nodes.summary: This text is from Turkey's After-Sales Services Regulation (Satış Sonrası Hizmetler Yönetmeliği), listing warranty periods, service point requirements across 7 geographic regions, and response times (20 or 45 working days) for numerous product categories. It covers: outboard marine engines (10 yr); home alternative energy systems (7 yr); electronics and telecommunications including phones, computers, peripherals, security systems, home electronics, cameras, and drones (3-10 yr); electric generating devices (3-10 yr); vehicles and spare parts (3-10 yr); home sewing machines; garden machines (5 yr); measuring instruments (5-10 yr); sports and hunting equipment (10 yr); home appliances, personal care products, and food preparation devices (5-10 yr); musical instruments (7 yr); wood/metal furniture (10 yr); and door/window systems (5-10 yr). Each item specifies whether service is required, the number of service points, and the maximum response time.

nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter of Turkey's Consumer Awards Regulation, covering purpose, scope, legal basis, and definitions. Article 1 states the regulation's aim is to protect and raise consumer awareness, encourage consumers to exercise their legal rights, and promote companies that consider consumer preferences as well as scientific studies in consumer law, by establishing procedures for consumer awards. Article 2 identifies the legal basis as Articles 60 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law (No. 6502, dated 7/11/2013). Article 3 provides definitions for key terms: Minister and Ministry (Customs and Trade), General Directorate and General Director (Consumer Protection and Market Surveillance), Provincial Trade Directorate, Selection Committee (decides award recipients), Consumer (natural or legal persons acting for non-commercial purposes), Consumer Award (awards given by the Ministry or other entities in various fields), and Consumer Organizations (associations, foundations, or umbrella bodies established for consumer protection).

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM Genel Esaslar
key_items: Başkan ve üyeler; Ödül töreninin yeri ve tarihi
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 2 (General Principles) of the Consumer Awards Regulation. Article 4 defines six award categories with specific criteria: Conscious Consumer, Written Press, Radio-Television Program, Consumer Satisfaction Company, Scientific Work, and Consumer Special Award. Article 5 permits award competitions in fields like caricature, short film, and design, with procedures, jury, and sponsorship arrangements set by the Ministry. Article 6 limits evaluation to the announcement year and caps awards at three per category. Article 7 establishes a Selection Committee for all awards except the Special Award, which the Minister determines. Article 8 specifies the seven-member committee composition, including representatives from YÖK, TOBB, TESK, and consumer organizations. Article 9 requires annual December announcements in a top-circulation newspaper and on the Ministry website. Article 10 grants the Ministry discretion over ceremony location and date. Article 11 states awards take the form of plaques, statuettes, or shields, and competition prizes should be encouraging.

nodes.title: Seçici Kurulun Çalışma Usul ve Esasları
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of the Consumer Awards Regulation, detailing the Selective Board's working procedures. Article 12 specifies meeting rules: the Board convenes within two months of the application deadline, requires at least five members including the chair, and decides by majority; the chair breaks ties. If the chair is absent, the General Manager presides. Members with a conflict of interest (themselves, descendants, ancestors, spouse, or relatives up to the third degree, including in-laws, being award candidates) must abstain from voting. Article 13 addresses decision notification: the Board communicates its decision and reasoning to the General Directorate, which then ensures the announcement to award recipients. Article 14 states that the Board's secretariat services are managed by the General Directorate.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text is the Fourth Chapter (Various and Final Provisions) of a Turkish Consumer Awards Regulation. Article 15 stipulates that consumer awards given by other natural or legal persons must be granted without any benefit and based on pre-announced objective criteria; technical measurements require accredited institutions or universities, while satisfaction/choice-based awards must rely on independent research institutions using scientific criteria. Article 16 states that Ministry-awarded prizes are funded from the Ministry's budget. Article 17 repeals the 2001 Traditional Consumer Awards Regulation (Official Gazette No. 24554). Article 18 specifies the regulation enters into force on its publication date. Article 19 assigns execution to the Minister of Customs and Trade. The regulation was published in Official Gazette No. 29043 on 27/11/2014 and amended by a regulation in Official Gazette No. 29218 on 27/12/2014.

nodes.title: TİCARİ REKLAM VE HAKSIZ TİCARİ UYGULAMALAR YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ KISIM
nodes.summary: This text is the first part of Turkey's Regulation on Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices (Official Gazette, Jan 10, 2015, No. 29232). It covers: (1) Purpose – establishing principles for advertisers, agencies, media organizations, and commercial practitioners, and protecting consumers from unfair practices; (2) Scope – all consumer-directed commercial advertising and unfair commercial practices; (3) Legal basis – Articles 61, 62, 63, and 84 of Consumer Protection Law No. 6502; (4) Definitions – defining over 20 key terms including subtitles, footnotes, static text, unfair influence, unfair commercial practice, service, permanent data storage, comparative advertising, goods, media, media organization, average consumer, covert advertising, advertising agency, advertiser, commercial advertising, commercial practitioner, consumer, and consumer-directed commercial practice.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ KISIM
Ticari Reklamlar BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Genel Esaslar
Basic Principles and Ad Distinction in Commercial Advertising Regulation
nodes.summary: This page from the Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation covers two articles under General Principles. Article 5 (Basic Principles) prohibits advertisements containing: content contrary to moral rules, harmful to public health, promoting violence or illegal acts, exploiting vulnerable groups (patients, children, elderly, disabled), discriminatory content based on race, gender, religion, etc., undermining human dignity, using private life images without consent, exploiting fears and superstitions, before/after patient treatment images, anxiety-inducing health-related content, or unsafe practices. Article 6 (Distinguishing Advertisements) requires ads to be clearly identifiable as such regardless of format or medium; prohibits subliminal advertising; mandates visual and auditory distinction from editorial content; and requires that ads using program-identifying elements (titles, logos, sets, music) or news/public service announcement imagery be easily recognizable as advertisements by consumers.

nodes.title: Doğruluk ve dürüstlük
nodes.summary: The text covers three articles from Turkey's Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation. Article 7 (Truthfulness and Honesty) requires ads to be truthful, socially responsible, and non-misleading regarding product/service characteristics, pricing, payment terms, warranties, IP rights, official recognitions, and consumer rights. It prohibits exploiting consumer trust, distorting research/statistics, or misusing mandatory licenses to imply superiority. Article 8 (Comparative Advertising) sets conditions: no competitor identifiers, no misleading content, same-need products, objective verifiable comparisons, scientific proof, no disparagement, no confusion, and compliance with Advertising Board rules. It restricts health/nutrition claim comparisons in food ads, bans comparative ads for dietary supplements, and prohibits price comparisons in regulated sectors. Article 9 (Burden of Proof) obligates advertisers to substantiate all claims with scientific evidence, requiring university or accredited institution documentation for comparative ads, with reports current to the ad's publication period, and mandates providing evidence to oversight authorities.

nodes.title: Comparative Advertising Conditions and Burden of Proof in Commercial Ads
nodes.summary: This page from the Regulation on Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices outlines conditions for comparative advertising: non-misleading content, no unfair competition, same needs/purpose, consumer benefit, objective comparison of material features, scientific proof for measurable claims, no competitor disparagement, same geographical origin, no brand/name confusion, and compliance with Advertising Board principles. It prohibits comparative advertising of health claims in food ads, bans supplementary food comparisons, and restricts price comparisons in regulated sectors. Article 9 (Burden of Proof) requires advertisers to substantiate all claims with scientifically valid evidence; comparative advertising claims must be proven via university or accredited body documents; reports must be valid during the ad's broadcast period; and advertisers must submit supporting documents to authorized oversight authorities upon request.

nodes.title: Advertising Regulations: Defamation, Unfair Reputation Use, and Imitation
nodes.summary: This page covers three advertising regulation provisions. Article 10 (Defamation) prohibits ads from demeaning, mocking, or disparaging any person, institution, commercial activity, product, service, advertisement, or brand. Article 11 (Unfair Benefit from Reputation) forbids using a person's or institution's name, emblem, logo, or identity elements in a misleading manner, and prohibits unfairly benefiting from a person's name, trade name, intellectual or industrial property rights, or reputation established through an ad campaign. Article 12 (Imitation) bars ads from imitating another advertisement's text, slogan, visual presentation, music, or sound effects in a way that misleads or confuses consumers, and prohibits presenting a product or service as an imitation or copy of one bearing a protected brand or trade name.

nodes.title: Fiyat bilgisi içeren reklamlar
nodes.summary: The text covers Turkish regulations on advertising (Articles 13-15 of the Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation). Article 13 governs price information in ads: prices must be relevant, complete (including all taxes), in Turkish Lira, with no misleading omissions; delivery costs, conditions for linked prices, installment details (total price, number, and amount), obligations for free goods, and validity/stock limits must be clearly stated. Article 14 regulates discounted sales ads: start/end dates, quantity limits, and no misleading discount impressions are required; discounts are calculated from the immediately preceding price, and the advertiser bears the burden of proof. Article 15 covers lottery, competition, and promotion ads: prizes must match promises and meet reasonable consumer expectations; gift quantities, validity periods, promotion dates, and delivery conditions must be disclosed; and organizers must ensure easy consumer access to promotions.

nodes.title: Regulations on Discount, Promotion, and Lottery Advertising
nodes.summary: This page covers provisions from the Turkish Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation. It addresses: (1) obligations consumers must fulfill for free goods/services must be stated in the ad's main message; (2) price validity periods and stock limits must be disclosed; (3) Article 14 on discount sales advertising—requiring clear start/end dates, quantity limits, prohibition of misleading discount expressions, calculation based on the immediately preceding price, and burden of proof on the advertiser; (4) Article 15 on lottery, competition, and promotion advertising—requiring prizes to meet reasonable consumer expectations, disclosure of gift quantities and validity periods, explanation of lottery/competition conditions and dates, and ensuring easy consumer access to promotions; (5) a repealed paragraph (Article 15(2)).

nodes.title: Regulations on Testimonial and Environmental Claims in Advertising
nodes.summary: The text covers two regulatory articles governing advertising. Article 16 (Testimonial Ads) prohibits false or unsubstantiated testimonials not based on real experience, knowledge, or research; bans expired or inapplicable approvals; and forbids any health-related claims or impressions by doctors, dentists, veterinarians, pharmacists, or health institutions regarding products or services. Article 17 (Environmental Claims in Ads) prohibits exploiting consumers' environmental sensitivity or knowledge gaps; bans deceptive use of environmental labels, symbols, and approvals; restricts environmental impact claims to scientifically validated findings accepted by academic institutions; and mandates stating the energy efficiency class in ads for products subject to compulsory energy labeling.

This section covers the General Principles of Turkey's Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation (Articles 5–17). It establishes prohibited ad content (moral violations, harm to vulnerable groups, discrimination, subliminal techniques) and requires ads to be clearly identifiable. It mandates truthfulness, honesty, and non-misleading representations of product characteristics, pricing, and warranties. Comparative advertising conditions are defined, including objective comparisons, scientific proof, and restrictions on health claims, supplements, and regulated-sector price comparisons. Advertisers bear the burden of proof with scientifically valid evidence. The section prohibits defamation, unfair exploitation of reputation or intellectual property, and imitation of other advertisements. It regulates price information (completeness, taxes, installments, validity), discount sales (dates, limits, calculation basis), and lottery/competition/promotion ads (prize disclosure, consumer access). Finally, it governs testimonial ads (banning false or health-related professional endorsements) and environmental claims (requiring scientific validation and prohibiting deceptive eco-labels).

This section (İKİNCİ KISIM) covers the General Principles of Turkey's Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation (Articles 5–17). It establishes prohibited advertising content (moral violations, harm to vulnerable groups, discrimination, subliminal techniques), mandates clear ad identification, truthfulness, and non-misleading representations. It defines conditions for comparative advertising, including objective comparisons, scientific proof, and restrictions on health claims and regulated-sector price comparisons. Advertisers bear the burden of proof. The section prohibits defamation, unfair exploitation of reputation or intellectual property, and imitation of other ads. It regulates price information completeness, discount sales parameters, and lottery/competition/promotion advertising requirements. Finally, it governs testimonial ads (banning false or health-related professional endorsements) and environmental claims (requiring scientific validation and prohibiting deceptive eco-labels).

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
Reklamlardaki Görseller ile Yazılı ve Sesli İfadeler
nodes.summary: This text covers Articles 18-21 of Turkey's Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation, addressing the presentation of visuals alongside written and audio expressions in advertisements. Article 18 requires that consumer-relevant information be perceivable, main promises be clearly stated, and that subtitles/footnotes be minimal, readable, and not contradict the main promise or negate its advantages. Article 19 specifies minimum text sizes for subtitles and static text across different TV formats (SDTV, HDTV, 4K) and print media (minimum Arial 8 point equivalent), with lowercase lettering rules and measurement standards. Article 20 mandates subtitle display duration based on word count (0.25 seconds per word plus additional time depending on total words), with rules for counting URLs and phone numbers. Article 21 sets requirements for contrast, background handling, prohibition of complex fonts/effects, proper spacing, safe-area positioning, and mutual visibility of text and visuals.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Örtülü Reklam
key_items: Aşırı tüketimi tavsiye edilmeyen gıdalara ilişkin reklamlar MADDE 24/A – (Ek:RG-28/12/2018-30639) (2)
nodes.summary: The text covers two chapters of Turkey's Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation. Chapter 3 (Covert Advertising) prohibits all forms of covert advertising in any media and bars using ads to compromise editorial independence. It sets evaluation criteria for brand/logo/trade name appearances in content, requiring proportionality, consumer information needs, and no steering of purchase decisions, with specific restrictions for tourism/folklore programs and urban/street/event settings. Chapter 4 (Children in Advertising) imposes extensive prohibitions on ads targeting or affecting children, including: no harmful content to physical/mental/moral development, no unrealistic expectations, no superiority or exclusion messages, no dangerous situations or violence, no exploitation of trust or parental authority, no direct persuasion to convince parents, no misleading price or affordability claims, and mandatory safety warnings. Article 24/A restricts advertising of red-category foods/drinks in children's media, requires balanced-nutrition disclaimers elsewhere, and bans giving child-targeted gifts to boost sales of such products.

This section covers regulations on visual, written, and audio elements in advertisements (Articles 18–21), including requirements for perceivability of consumer information, minimum text sizes across TV and print formats, subtitle display duration rules, and visual presentation standards such as contrast, font restrictions, spacing, and safe-area positioning. It also addresses covert advertising prohibitions, evaluation criteria for brand/logo/trade name appearances in content, and restrictions on steering purchase decisions. Additionally, it covers extensive protections for children in advertising, prohibiting harmful content, unrealistic expectations, exploitation of trust or parental authority, dangerous situations, misleading price claims, and direct persuasion tactics. Specific restrictions apply to advertising red-category foods and drinks in children's media, requiring balanced-nutrition disclaimers and banning child-targeted gifts to boost sales of such products.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: Chapter 5 of the Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices Regulation covers additional advertising rules. Article 25 governs financial services ads, requiring accurate interest/profit rates, clear total credit costs, and prohibiting misleading information on credit terms. Article 26 mandates that ads for pharmaceuticals, medical products, food, cosmetics, tobacco, and alcoholic beverages comply with their specific sector regulations. Article 27 addresses: direct sales/telemarketing requirements (seller info, total price, cancellation rights, no urgency tactics); prohibition on advertising vacation services as investments; ban on ads for fortune tellers, mediums, and illegal gambling; restrictions on installment/rental sale ads; mandatory gross/net area disclosure in real estate ads; obligation to disclose ingredients conflicting with religious sensitivities; electronic communication service ad rules (speed/coverage disclaimers, test-condition labeling, fair usage limits); prohibition on chat/dating line ads; and a ban on firearm advertising except in corporate websites, fairs, and specialized hunting/shooting media.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ KISIM
MADDE 28
nodes.summary: This text is Article 28 of a Turkish regulation on Unfair Commercial Practices (Part Three). It defines unfair commercial practices as those directed at consumers that fail to meet professional diligence standards and significantly distort or risk distorting the economic behavior of the average consumer or targeted group regarding a product or service. Unfair practices are prohibited before, during, or after a consumer transaction. It establishes that practices reducing a consumer's informed decision-making ability, causing them to enter transactions they would not normally enter, constitute significant distortion. For vulnerable consumer groups (due to mental/physical weaknesses, age, or inexperience), the impact on economic behavior is assessed based on the group's average member. Finally, it states that misleading actions (Art. 29), misleading omissions (Art. 30), aggressive commercial practices (Art. 31), and those listed in the Annex are always deemed unfair commercial practices.

nodes.title: Aldatıcı eylemler
nodes.summary: The text covers three articles from Turkey's Regulation on Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices. Article 29 defines misleading actions: commercial practices that deceive or may deceive the average consumer into entering a legal transaction, listing specific areas of potential deception including product/service characteristics, trader commitments, pricing, consumer rights, after-sales services, and trader identity/qualifications. It also addresses confusion with competitors and non-compliance with professional body rules. Article 30 defines misleading omissions: hiding important information, presenting offers incomprehensibly or at inappropriate times, or concealing the purpose of a practice, with provisions for communication medium limitations. Article 31 defines aggressive commercial practices involving harassment, coercion, or undue influence that impairs consumer freedom of choice, listing assessment factors such as timing, threats, exploitation of disasters, disproportionate barriers to contract termination, and threats of unlawful acts.

nodes.title: Misleading Omissions and Aggressive Commercial Practices in Turkish Regulation
nodes.summary: This page from the Turkish Regulation on Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices covers: (1) the tail end of misleading practices criteria, including confusion with competitors' goods, brands, or distinguishing features, and failure to comply with professional body rules; (2) Article 30 on misleading omissions, defining them as hiding material information, presenting offers incomprehensibly or at inappropriate times, or concealing the purpose of a practice, causing the average consumer to enter a legal transaction they would not otherwise enter, with assessment considering communication medium limitations and alternative information channels; (3) Article 31 on aggressive commercial practices, defining them as harassment, coercion, physical violence, or undue influence that significantly impairs consumer choice, with evaluation factors including time, place, nature, and continuity of the practice; presence of threats or insults; exploitation of natural disasters or crises; disproportionate obstacles to exercising contractual rights; and threats of unlawful acts.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ KISIM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers Part Four (Various and Final Provisions) of a Turkish regulation on commercial advertising. Article 32 states that correcting or compensating non-compliant advertising or commercial practices does not eliminate the advertiser's liability for the violation. Article 33 repeals the 2003 regulation on Commercial Advertising and Announcements. Article 34 specifies the regulation enters into force on its publication date (amended in 2018). Article 35 assigns execution authority to the Minister of Customs and Trade. A 2018 amendment added a clause to Article 8, effective June 30, 2019. The text also lists the original publication in the Official Gazette (January 10, 2015, No. 29232) and enumerates six subsequent amendments with their respective dates and gazette numbers, spanning from December 2015 to October 2019.

nodes.title: -EK-
nodes.summary:
Ticari Reklam ve Haksız Ticari Uygulamalar Yönetmeliği
-EK-

This section (Part Three) of Turkey's Regulation on Commercial Advertising and Unfair Commercial Practices defines unfair commercial practices (Art. 28) as those failing professional diligence standards that distort consumer economic behavior, with special provisions for vulnerable groups. It details misleading actions (Art. 29) covering deception about product characteristics, pricing, and trader identity; misleading omissions (Art. 30) involving hidden material information or incomprehensible offers; and aggressive practices (Art. 31) including harassment, coercion, and undue influence. Part Four (Various and Final Provisions) establishes that correction does not eliminate liability (Art. 32), repeals the 2003 regulation (Art. 33), specifies entry into force (Art. 34), assigns execution to the Minister of Customs and Trade (Art. 35), and records the original 2015 publication plus six amendments through 2019. The section concludes with a reference to the Annex.

nodes.title: HAKSIZ TİCARİ UYGULAMA OLARAK KABUL EDİLEN ÖRNEK UYGULAMALAR
A - Aldatıcı Ticari Uygulamalar
nodes.summary: The text lists 20 examples of deceptive commercial practices deemed unfair under Turkish consumer protection regulations. These include: falsely claiming membership in professional bodies or using unauthorized quality/environmental marks; falsely asserting institutional approval of practices or products; bait-and-switch tactics (inviting purchases at a price then refusing to fulfill); creating artificial urgency; falsely claiming legality; presenting consumer rights as product features; threatening consumers; falsely claiming business closure or relocation; claiming products aid in games of chance; making unauthorized health claims; misleading about market conditions; offering unspecified prizes; labeling paid goods as 'free'; falsely denying commercial capacity; misleading about after-sales service abroad; unjustified price increases disguised as cost-driven (added 2018); and misleading packaging that conceals changes in unit-measurement elements like weight or volume (added 2021).

nodes.title: B - Saldırgan Ticari Uygulamalar
nodes.summary: The text outlines five types of aggressive commercial practices (Saldırgan Ticari Uygulamalar) under Turkish consumer law: (1) creating the impression that a consumer cannot leave a business premises until a legal relationship is established; (2) persistently visiting a consumer's home despite explicit warnings to stop and not return; (3) demanding irrelevant documents, fees, or systematically avoiding discussions to deter consumers from exercising their legal rights; (4) pressuring consumers by claiming the business's livelihood is at risk if they do not purchase the product or service; and (5) creating false impressions about winning rewards or benefits that do not actually exist, requiring payment or expense to obtain them.

nodes.title: Advertising Board Regulation: Purpose, Scope, Basis, and Definitions
nodes.summary: This page from the Advertising Board Regulation (Official Gazette No. 29049, 3 July 2014) covers Section 1. Article 1 defines the regulation's purpose: organizing the establishment, duties, working procedures, secretariat services, and other matters of the Advertising Board and its specialized committees. Article 2 states the legal basis as Articles 63 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 (7 November 2013). Article 3 provides definitions for key terms used throughout the regulation, including: Minister and Ministry (Customs and Trade), Chairman, General Director and General Directorate (Consumer Protection and Market Surveillance), unfair commercial practice, the Law, Committee and Committee Chairman, Board, commercial advertisement, and Member.

nodes.title: Reklam Kurulunun Kuruluş ve Görevleri
nodes.summary: This text covers the establishment, membership qualifications, term, and duties of the Turkish Advertising Council (Reklam Kurulu). Article 4 defines the Council's composition of 19 members (including the chair) appointed from various ministries, RTÜK, Turkish Standards Institute, municipalities, YÖK, TOBB, consumer organizations, advertiser/advertising associations, and professional unions (pharmacists, dentists, doctors, lawyers). Article 5 sets member qualifications: Turkish citizenship, minimum two-year college education, compliance with Civil Servants Law conditions, and no deprivation of public rights. Article 6 specifies a three-year renewable term, with vacancies filled within one month and new members completing the predecessor's remaining term. Article 7 outlines the Council's duties: establishing advertising principles and consumer protection regulations, examining and inspecting commercial ads and unfair practices, applying administrative sanctions, criteria for determining national vs. local scope of violations, delegation of suspension authority to the Chair, and consideration of universal standards and developments in setting principles.

This section covers example practices deemed unfair commercial practices under Turkish consumer law, divided into two categories: deceptive practices (20 examples including false claims of institutional approval, bait-and-switch tactics, artificial urgency, unauthorized health claims, misleading packaging, and unjustified price increases) and aggressive practices (5 types including trapping consumers in premises, persistent unwanted home visits, demanding irrelevant documents to deter rights exercise, pressuring via livelihood claims, and false reward impressions). Additionally, the section addresses the Advertising Board Regulation (Official Gazette No. 29049), detailing its purpose, legal basis (Consumer Protection Law No. 6502), and key definitions. It further describes the Advertising Council's establishment, including its 19-member composition from various institutions, member qualifications, three-year renewable terms, and duties such as setting advertising principles, examining commercial ads, applying administrative sanctions, and determining violation scope.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
Reklam Kurulunun Çalışma Usul ve Esasları
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 of the Advertising Board Regulation, detailing the Board's working procedures. It addresses: (1) Applications – written/electronic submissions with required identification details, complaint specifics for advertising and unfair commercial practices, and attachment of ad originals or images; (2) Meetings – minimum monthly frequency, quorum of 11 members, majority voting with President's tie-break, Vice-president substitution, absence notification, automatic membership termination for repeated absences, and conflict-of-interest recusal rules; (3) Agenda and discussion renewal – set by President, renewable upon request of at least 3 members; (4) Representation – by the President; (5) Investigation – requesting documents from relevant parties within 15 days and consulting specialized experts; (6) Implementation and publication of decisions by the Ministry; (7) President's duties – overseeing tasks, initiating inspections, presiding meetings, and managing secretariat; (8) Secretariat services – preparation, notifications, filing, minutes, and correspondence; (9) Minutes – recording and signing of all meeting discussions and decisions.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM İhtisas Komisyonları
nodes.summary: This text covers the Fourth Chapter of a regulation on Specialized Committees (İhtisas Komisyonları). It addresses: (1) Establishment – the Ministry creates sectoral committees of 3–5 members (including a chair) to assist the Board in decision-making, with members appointed by the Board; (2) Member qualifications – members must satisfy the conditions set out in Article 5; (3) Duties – committees examine assigned files and topics they deem necessary, conducting research and submitting their opinions as a report to the Advertising Board Presidency; (4) Meetings – committees meet at least monthly or whenever the Chair calls, deciding by majority of attendees, with the Chair's vote breaking ties; absent members must notify the Chair in writing or electronically beforehand; and membership is automatically terminated if a member misses two consecutive meetings or four meetings within a year without valid justification.

nodes.title: BEŞİNCİ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: The text covers two regulatory sections. First, the final chapter of the Advertising Council Regulation includes: financial provisions (expenses funded by the Ministry budget; honoraria for board and committee members set with Finance Ministry approval); repeal of the previous Advertising Council Regulation (2003); entry into force upon publication; and execution by the Minister of Customs and Trade. Second, the Consumer Council Regulation's first chapter defines: its purpose (regulating the Consumer Council's establishment, duties, meetings, and working procedures); its legal basis (Articles 64 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502, dated 7/11/2013); and definitions of key terms including Minister, Ministry, Deputy Minister, Chairman, General Directorate, General Director, Law, Council, Undersecretary, Consumer Organizations (associations, foundations, or their umbrella bodies), and Member.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM Kuruluş ve Görevler
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 2 (Establishment and Duties) of the Consumer Council Regulation. It covers: (1) Establishment of the Consumer Council to identify consumer needs, protect interests, and communicate law-related views to authorities, meeting at least annually under Ministry coordination. (2) Council composition, chaired by the Minister or a designated official, with representatives from numerous ministries, regulatory bodies, professional associations, unions, municipalities, and consumer organizations. (3) Selection criteria for consumer association representatives, including document submission deadlines, minimum one-year existence requirement, active status, and allocation of 20 seats based on membership size. (4) Council duties: researching consumer needs, resolving problems, forming opinions on legislation, monitoring developments, suggesting educational materials, selecting an Advertising Board member, and other tasks. (5) President's duties: presiding, setting agendas, evaluating reports, ensuring efficient operations, and representing the Council. (6) Secretariat services handled by the General Directorate, including preparations, archiving, notifications, and communicating decisions.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Çalışma Usul ve Esasları
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 (Working Procedures and Principles) of the Consumer Council Regulation, detailing: (1) Meeting format (Art. 11): the Council meets at least annually, with extraordinary meetings callable by the President or one-fourth of members via written justified request within two months; invitations with agenda sent at least one month prior. (2) Quorum (Art. 12): requires a majority of members; if unmet, a second meeting within two months proceeds without quorum. (3) Voting (Art. 13): decisions by majority of those present, with the President breaking ties; open voting; decisions recorded in minutes. (4) Agenda (Art. 14): set by the President; items may be added by written request from at least five represented organizations with member approval; agenda includes selecting a vice president and two secretaries, authorizing minutes, reviewing reports, selecting an Advertising Board member from consumer organization representatives, and other consumer protection matters. (5) Board composition and duties (Art. 15): the Board consists of the President, vice president, and two secretaries; responsible for managing meetings, counting votes, announcing decisions, and ensuring minutes are recorded.

nodes.title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text is the Fourth Chapter (Various and Final Provisions) of a Turkish regulation. It covers four articles: Article 16 states that expenses from implementing the Regulation are funded from the Ministry's budget; Article 17 repeals the Consumer Council Regulation published on 1/8/2003 in Official Gazette No. 25186; Article 18 specifies the Regulation enters into force on its publication date; and Article 19 assigns execution authority to the Minister of Customs and Trade. The text also references the Advertising Council Regulation (Reklam Konseyi Yönetmeliği) dated December 24, 2014, published in Official Gazette No. 29215.

nodes.title: REKLAM KONSEYİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM Amaç, Dayanak ve Tanımlar
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter (Purpose, Legal Basis, and Definitions) of the Advertising Council Regulation (Reklam Konseyi Yönetmeliği). It covers three main points: (1) Purpose: The regulation aims to establish the organization, duties, and working procedures of the Advertising Council. (2) Legal Basis: It is prepared based on Articles 65 and 84 of the Consumer Protection Law No. 6502, dated November 7, 2013. (3) Definitions: It defines key terms used throughout the regulation, including Minister, Deputy Minister, and Ministry (all referring to the Ministry of Customs and Trade), Chairman (Council Chairman), General Director and General Directorate (Consumer Protection and Market Surveillance), the Law (No. 6502), the Council (Advertising Council), Undersecretary, and Member (Advertising Council member).

This section covers multiple Turkish consumer protection regulations. It details the Advertising Board's working procedures: application handling, meeting rules (quorum, voting, recusal), agenda management, investigation powers, decision implementation, President's duties, secretariat services, and minutes. It establishes Specialized Committees (3-5 members) for sectoral advisory, with meeting and membership rules. It outlines the Consumer Council's purpose, legal basis (Law No. 6502), definitions, establishment, composition (representatives from ministries, associations, consumer organizations), duties, President's duties, and secretariat. It specifies the Consumer Council's working procedures: annual meetings, quorum, voting, agenda, and Board composition. It includes final provisions for both regulations (funding, repeal of 2003 regulations, entry into force, execution authority). Finally, it presents the Advertising Council Regulation's purpose, legal basis, and key term definitions.

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 2 of the Advertising Council Regulation, covering the Council's establishment, composition, and duties. Article 4 defines the Council's purpose: tracking modern communication practices, conducting research on advertising and supervision, and submitting opinions to authorities. Article 5 details its composition, chaired by the Minister or a designated official, with representatives from numerous ministries (Family, Economy, Interior, Culture, Finance, Education, Health, Treasury), regulatory bodies (Competition, Energy, Tobacco, Banking, IT), academic institutions, the Advertising Board, self-regulation bodies, and various industry associations (advertisers, TOBB, TESK, banks, consumer groups, press). Article 6 sets requirements for association representatives, including document submission, annual membership reporting, and a minimum one-year existence criterion. Article 7 outlines Council duties: monitoring international developments, forming working groups, raising public awareness, and developing measurement recommendations. Articles 8-10 specify the Chair's responsibilities (presiding, scheduling, evaluating reports) and the Secretariat's administrative functions (preparation, record-keeping, communication, and documentation) managed by the General Directorate.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
key_items: Reklam Konseyinin Çalışma Usul ve Esasları
DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
nodes.summary: This text covers Chapter 3 (Working Procedures of the Advertising Council) and Chapter 4 (Miscellaneous and Final Provisions) of a Turkish regulation. Chapter 3 details: meeting frequency (at least annually, coordinated by the Ministry) and 15-day advance notice (Art. 11); quorum requirements (majority of members, with a second meeting within two months if not met) (Art. 12); decision-making by majority vote of present members, with the President breaking ties, open voting, and recording by the board (Art. 13); agenda determination by the President, with additions possible via written requests from at least five represented institutions, and specific agenda items (Art. 14); board composition (President, vice president, two secretaries) and duties including managing sessions, counting votes, and recording minutes (Art. 15); and formation of working groups from members or experts, coordinated by a General Directorate representative, submitting reports to the General Directorate (Art. 16). Chapter 4 specifies that expenses are funded from the Ministry budget (Art. 17), the regulation enters into force on January 1, 2015 (Art. 18), and is executed by the Minister of Customs and Trade (Art. 19).

nodes.title: TÜKETİCİ HAKEM HEYETLERİ YÖNETMELİĞİ BİRİNCİ BÖLÜM
nodes.summary: This text is the first chapter (General Provisions) of the Consumer Arbitration Committees Regulation. It covers: (1) Purpose – regulating the establishment and operational procedures of consumer arbitration committees; (2) Scope – encompassing the work and operations of these committees for resolving disputes from consumer transactions and consumer-oriented practices; (3) Legal basis – Articles 72 and 84 of Law No. 6502 (Consumer Protection Law, 7/11/2013); and (4) Definitions – defining key terms including Ministry, Chairman, General Directorate, consumer arbitration committee, service, provincial directorate, Law, goods (movable property, residential/vacation real estate, electronic goods), provider, seller, consumer, Consumer Information System, consumer transaction (covering contracts such as works, transport, brokerage, insurance, agency, banking), and consumer organizations (associations, foundations, or their umbrella bodies).

nodes.title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM
Kuruluş, Görev ve Yetki Alanı
nodes.summary: This text is Chapter 2 of the Consumer Arbitration Boards Regulation, covering establishment, duties, and jurisdiction. Article 5 states the Ministry establishes at least one consumer arbitration board in provincial and designated district centers to resolve consumer transaction disputes, considering application volume, population density, and geography. Article 6 defines monetary jurisdiction limits: district boards handle disputes under 2,000 TL; provincial boards handle 2,000–3,000 TL in metropolitan cities, under 3,000 TL in non-metropolitan centers, and 2,000–3,000 TL in their districts. Disputes exceeding these limits cannot be filed with arbitration boards. Limits are adjusted annually per the revaluation rate. Boards must accept in-jurisdiction applications and return out-of-jurisdiction ones, indicating proper venues. Article 7 specifies that provincial boards operate within province boundaries and district boards within district boundaries. Applications may be filed at the consumer's residence or transaction location. Where no board exists, consumers may apply to the district governorship, which forwards the case to the designated board.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Başkan, Üye ve Raportör
Başkan ve üyeler
nodes.summary: This text covers Article 8 of a regulation on Consumer Arbitration Boards (Tüketici Hakem Heyeti). It specifies that the board is presided over by the provincial director or district governor (or their appointee) and consists of five members: one appointed by the mayor from expert municipal staff, one from the Bar Association, one from the Chamber of Commerce/Industry or Chamber of Artisans (depending on the dispute type), and one selected by consumer organizations. Alternates are designated by relevant institutions. If the president is absent, the bar representative presides. Unfilled positions are filled by state officials meeting Article 9 criteria. Non-president members serve three-year terms and may be reappointed. Vacancies due to resignation, death, prolonged illness, or other causes are filled by alternates completing the remaining term, with the outgoing member's status continuing until the successor assumes duty. Finally, board members may not serve on more than one Consumer Arbitration Board simultaneously.

nodes.title: Üyelerde aranacak şartlar
nodes.summary: Article 9 outlines the mandatory conditions for consumer arbitration committee members: Turkish citizenship, being at least 18 years old, meeting specific Civil Servants Law (No. 657) requirements, not being deprived of public rights, having no mental illness preventing continuous duty, and holding at least a four-year university degree. Where four-year graduates are unavailable, members may be appointed from vocational school or high school graduates in provinces, or at least primary school graduates in districts. Graduates of institutions with equivalency recognized by YÖK or the Ministry of Education are also eligible. If a member is later found to have lost or never met these conditions, their duty terminates from the date of discovery, the relevant institution is notified, and the reserve member assumes the role to complete the remaining term.

nodes.title: Tüketici örgütleri temsilcisinin tespiti
nodes.summary: The text covers Turkish Consumer Arbitration Board regulations, including: (1) Selection of consumer organization representatives—eligibility based on location, voting rules among organizations, selection criteria (active presence, member count, branch count), notification deadlines, and procedures when no organization exists or one is established later. (2) Application procedures—filing in person, via lawyer, by mail, or electronically through e-Devlet/Consumer Information System; required information; currency conversion rules; and prohibition of duplicate filings. (3) Mandatory use of the Consumer Information System for all records, with fallback to manual filing if the system is unavailable. (4) Authority to request information/documents from parties and institutions, with a 30-day response deadline and decision based on existing evidence if unmet. (5) Meeting logistics—minimum twice monthly, location set by provincial/district authorities, agenda set by the chair. (6) Quorum (minimum 3 members including chair), majority voting, no abstentions, and chair's tie-breaking vote.

nodes.title: Consumer Arbitration Board Procedures: System Use, Meetings, and Decisions
nodes.summary: The text covers regulations for Turkish Consumer Arbitration Boards. It mandates that electronic applications must be submitted via the Consumer Information System with complete forms and uploaded documents, and prohibits duplicate filings for the same dispute. Article 11/A requires all board operations to be recorded in the system, with manual submissions accepted only when the system is unavailable. Article 12 grants the board authority to request any relevant information or documents from parties or institutions, with a 30-day response deadline (extendable), and decisions based on existing evidence if deadlines are missed. Article 13 sets meeting frequency (minimum twice monthly), triggered by the chair, held in designated provincial or district locations, and only when disputes are on the agenda. Article 14 states the chair determines and communicates the agenda before meetings. Article 15 establishes a quorum of at least three members including the chair, majority-vote decisions, prohibition of abstentions, and the chair's vote breaking ties.

nodes.title: Consumer Arbitration Committee: Attendance, Conflicts, and Examination
nodes.summary: The text covers three articles from the Consumer Arbitration Committees Regulation. Article 16 mandates member attendance at meetings, requiring written or email notification to the chair for valid absences; membership is revoked after four consecutive unexcused absences or absence from all meetings in a three-month period, with a one-year ban on reappointment. Article 17 lists conflict-of-interest situations (spouse, descendants/ancestors, fiancé, adoption, third-degree blood or affinity relations, acting as legal representative, or being a party) that prevent the chair and members from attending related dispute meetings. Article 18 states that the committee conducts its examination through the rapporteur's report and case file, and may additionally hear the parties and expert witnesses if deemed necessary.

This section covers the composition, qualifications, and operational procedures of Turkish Consumer Arbitration Boards. It defines the board's structure (president and five members from municipal, bar, chamber, and consumer organization representatives), three-year terms, vacancy procedures, and prohibition on dual membership. It specifies mandatory member qualifications (citizenship, age, education, legal eligibility) and termination provisions. The section details consumer organization representative selection, application filing methods, and mandatory use of the Consumer Information System. It establishes the board's authority to request documents (30-day deadline), meeting frequency (minimum twice monthly), quorum (three members including chair), majority voting with chair's tie-breaking vote, and prohibition of abstentions. Finally, it addresses attendance obligations with revocation penalties, conflict-of-interest recusal grounds, and examination through rapporteur reports and case files, with optional party and witness hearings.

This section of the Consumer Arbitration Boards Regulation covers the establishment, duties, and jurisdiction of consumer arbitration boards, including monetary limits (district boards under 2,000 TL; provincial boards 2,000–3,000 TL), geographic boundaries, and application filing procedures. It further details the board's composition (president and five members from municipal, bar, chamber, and consumer organization representatives), three-year terms, mandatory qualifications, and operational rules such as quorum, majority voting with chair's tie-breaking vote, meeting frequency, document request authority, conflict-of-interest recusal, and rapporteur-based case examination. Finally, it addresses expert (bilirkişi) examination provisions, though most related articles have been repealed, with remaining changes effective from 1 January 2021.

nodes.title: ALTINCI BÖLÜM
Tüketici Hakem Heyeti Kararı
nodes.summary: This text covers Articles 22-28 of the Consumer Arbitration Board Regulation, addressing: (1) Decision nature and scope—board is bound by parties' requests, may deviate if amount was undeterminable at filing, must respect monetary limits, can combine related disputes within jurisdiction, amounts in Turkish Lira, expert/notification fees specified, decision binds parties only for that dispute, lawyer representation allowed without fee awards, and mootness if resolved pre-decision; (2) Decision deadline—6 months, extendable by 6 more, urgent prioritization, foreign consumers treated urgently; (3) Decision record—signed, archived, with minimum content requirements (parties, request, amount, reasoning, decision, fees, objection info); (4) Notification—within 10 business days via registered mail or courier; (5) Enforcement per Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law; (6) Correction of obvious errors ex officio or on request; (7) Objection—15 days to consumer court, doesn't halt enforcement unless ordered, court decision is final, transmitted via National Judiciary Network, and attorney fees awarded if consumer's favorable decision is overturned.

nodes.title: YEDİNCİ BÖLÜM Çeşitli ve Son Hükümler
key_items: Yürürlükten kaldırılan yönetmelik; Henüz karara bağlanmamış başvurular GEÇİCİ MADDE 2 – (Ek:RG-11/8/2017- 30151
